chapters.title: Chapter 66: Hell Difficulty Blood Moon Cathedral, Moon Sect Devouts
paragraphs: After leaving Tolkien behind in his blacksmith shop, Leon and Emilia stepped back into the streets and immediately picked up their pace.
They moved quickly, weaving through the dimly lit roads of [Moon City], careful but not hesitant.
Thankfully, they didn’t encounter any [Moon Sect Guards] on the way.
After his reputation with the Moon Sect had dropped to zero, any guard who spotted him would attack without hesitation.
Leon didn’t mind fighting them, but unnecessary battles would only waste time and stamina, both of which mattered right now.
The [Blood Moon] event had already begun. Time was ticking.
Eventually, the massive silhouette of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] appeared before them once more, looming over the city like a dark omen.
The area around it was crowded.

Tens of thousands of players from all races were gathered nearby, most of them standing in groups, discussing strategies, checking their stats, or simply staring at the massive structure in front of them.
No one was in a rush. After all, the [Blood Moon] would last for twenty-four hours.
Rushing blindly into a high-risk dungeon was the fastest way to get wiped out.
For most players, caution was the right choice.
But Leon wasn’t most players. He had a secret quest with a time limit.
And most importantly, he didn’t want to stay in one place long enough for the Moon Sect to reorganize and come after him.
So while others hesitated, Leon pushed forward.
He and Emilia slipped through the crowd, ignoring the curious glances and whispered comments.
Fwoosh!
They reached the cathedral’s entrance, and the familiar system panel appeared before Leon’s eyes.
[Which difficulty do you wish to choose?]
[Normal] [Hard] [Hell]
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
Unlike previous dungeons, there was no [Easy] difficulty. That alone spoke volumes.
And this was also the first dungeon he had seen in this life that offered [Hell] difficulty.
A difficulty so brutal that almost no one dared to choose it.
If Leon remembered correctly, most players needed at least 40,000 Combat Power just to attempt it, and even then, survival wasn’t guaranteed.
But Leon wasn’t here to play it safe. The quest description was clear.
The "terrifying force" was sealed inside the deepest part of the cathedral.
And that place was only accessible through the hardest difficulty. Leon didn’t hesitate.
Ding!
[Blood Moon Cathedral (Hell Difficulty) has been selected.]
[Party of 2 detected: Celestial and Saintess.]
[May the will of the "Heavenly One" be with you.]
"...Damn," Emilia muttered under her breath.
Leon smirked faintly. Whenever the system included a line like that, it usually meant one thing: you’re about to suffer.
Still, Leon felt confident. Without any further delay, the two stepped forward.
Their surroundings blurred for a split second.
Fwish!
And then—
They were inside. The interior of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] was enormous.
Far larger than the outside suggested. The ceiling stretched impossibly high, supported by massive black pillars carved with twisted symbols.
Shadows crawled across the stone like living things, warping and shifting as if reacting to their presence.
Crimson light seeped in through tall, narrow windows lining the walls, bathing everything in an eerie red glow.
The air itself felt heavy. Oppressive.
"This place is..." Emilia swallowed, her face paling slightly. "Creepy."
Leon didn’t respond. He simply stepped forward, eyes scanning the surroundings, senses sharpened.
The [Hell] difficulty wasn’t going to ease them in.
They advanced deeper into the cathedral, their footsteps echoing faintly against the stone floor.
The silence was unsettling.
And then—
Fwish!
A sphere of crimson light shot straight toward them.
"Move!" Leon barked.
They both dodged instinctively.
BOOM!
The orb slammed into the ground where they had been standing, erupting in a violent explosion that shook the entire area around them.
"What the hell?!" Emilia lifted her scepter instantly.
Before either of them could speak again, more crimson orbs began forming in the darkness ahead.
Figures emerged alongside them.
[Moon Sect Devout]
[Level: 25]
[Exclusive Talent: Blood Moon Worshipper (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 30,000]
[Details: Devouts of the "Blood Moon" sect, currently searching for the force hidden deep within the cathedral.]
Emilia’s eyes widened.
"All of them have thirty thousand combat power?!" she exclaimed. "Holy hell... even I couldn’t beat one of these by myself!"
"They can’t hurt you," Leon said calmly as he took his stance. "And for me..."
His grip tightened around his sword.
"They’re weak."
Fwish!
Leon activated [Vision Enhancement], his perception sharpening instantly.
At the same time, [Darkness Barrier] enveloped his body in a thin, shifting veil of black energy.
The devouts raised their scepters in unison, crimson energy gathering at their tips.
Leon moved first.
Slash!
He cut through the incoming orbs with precise swings, the explosions dispersing harmlessly as their cores were destroyed mid-air.
In the next instant, Leon raised his staff.
Storm of Lightning!
A violent storm erupted above the devouts, bolts of lightning crashing down relentlessly.
The moment the lightning struck, all of them stiffened, their bodies locking up as electricity coursed through them.
"Now!" Leon shouted.
Spectral Flames!
Emilia’s magic surged forward, ghostly flames engulfing the stunned devouts.
They didn’t even have time to scream. The combined assault wiped them out instantly.
Ding!
[You have killed x7 "Moon Sect Devout" and gained 14,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 18!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes and 100 free points to distribute.]
Leon felt a surge of power flow through his body.
Emilia did as well, her expression lighting up as she felt her own strength increase.
"Nice," Leon said with a grin. "Since the enemies here are far above our level, we’ll level up fast."
Emilia nodded eagerly. "This place is dangerous... but it’s perfect for growth."
Leon quickly checked the drops.
[Moon Sect Devout Robe x7 (Uncommon): +300 Defense, +150 Constitution, +100 Spirit. Requirement: 1,500 Spirit.]
[Moon Sect Scepter x7 (Rare): +500 Magic Attack, +400 Spirit, +200 Agility. Requirement: 1,000 Spirit.]
Without hesitation, Leon began fusing them.
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipment... enhancement successful!]
He repeated the process until only two items remained: [Moon Sect Devout Robe +3] and [Moon Sect Scepter +2]
Leon handed both to Emilia.
"These are way better than what you’re using," he said.
"Thanks!" Emilia beamed as she equipped them, her stats rising noticeably.
As they continued deeper into the cathedral, Leon spoke again.
"Focus mainly on your [Constitution] and [Spirit]. You don’t need agility if you can tank everything, and strength is pointless for you."
Emilia nodded, "Got it."
They moved forward once more. More Moon Sect Devouts appeared along the way, but none of them posed a real threat.
Even with 30,000 combat power, they couldn’t break through Leon’s attacks or even approach Emilia.
Still, Leon remained cautious. This was [Hell] difficulty. Something worse was coming.
And sure enough, only about ten minutes after entering the cathedral...
Fwish!
Leon spun around just in time to see a dark figure materialize behind Emilia.
A dagger flashed through the air, aimed straight at her back. Leon didn’t even bother to move even though he saw it though.
’That shoul make more confident in herself,’ he thought.
Because—
Slash! Clang!
The dagger struck Emilia... and bounced off harmlessly.
The figure froze in confusion. And before it could react again, Leon rushed forward.

sentences.text: After leaving Tolkien behind in his blacksmith shop, Leon and Emilia stepped back into the streets and immediately picked up their pace.
They moved quickly, weaving through the dimly lit roads of [Moon City], careful but not hesitant.
Thankfully, they didn’t encounter any [Moon Sect Guards] on the way.
After his reputation with the Moon Sect had dropped to zero, any guard who spotted him would attack without hesitation.
Leon didn’t mind fighting them, but unnecessary battles would only waste time and stamina, both of which mattered right now.
The [Blood Moon] event had already begun.
Time was ticking.
Eventually, the massive silhouette of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] appeared before them once more, looming over the city like a dark omen.
The area around it was crowded.

Tens of thousands of players from all races were gathered nearby, most of them standing in groups, discussing strategies, checking their stats, or simply staring at the massive structure in front of them.
No one was in a rush.
After all, the [Blood Moon] would last for twenty-four hours.
Rushing blindly into a high-risk dungeon was the fastest way to get wiped out.
For most players, caution was the right choice.
But Leon wasn’t most players.
He had a secret quest with a time limit.
And most importantly, he didn’t want to stay in one place long enough for the Moon Sect to reorganize and come after him.
So while others hesitated, Leon pushed forward.
He and Emilia slipped through the crowd, ignoring the curious glances and whispered comments.
Fwoosh!
They reached the cathedral’s entrance, and the familiar system panel appeared before Leon’s eyes.
[Which difficulty do you wish to choose?]
[Normal] [Hard] [Hell]
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
Unlike previous dungeons, there was no [Easy] difficulty.
That alone spoke volumes.
And this was also the first dungeon he had seen in this life that offered [Hell] difficulty.
A difficulty so brutal that almost no one dared to choose it.
If Leon remembered correctly, most players needed at least 40,000 Combat Power just to attempt it, and even then, survival wasn’t guaranteed.
But Leon wasn’t here to play it safe.
The quest description was clear.
The "terrifying force" was sealed inside the deepest part of the cathedral.
And that place was only accessible through the hardest difficulty.
Leon didn’t hesitate.
Ding!
[Blood Moon Cathedral (Hell Difficulty) has been selected.]
[Party of 2 detected: Celestial and Saintess.]
[May the will of the "Heavenly One" be with you.]
"...Damn," Emilia muttered under her breath.
Leon smirked faintly.
Whenever the system included a line like that, it usually meant one thing: you’re about to suffer.
Still, Leon felt confident.
Without any further delay, the two stepped forward.
Their surroundings blurred for a split second.
Fwish!
And then—
They were inside.
The interior of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] was enormous.
Far larger than the outside suggested.
The ceiling stretched impossibly high, supported by massive black pillars carved with twisted symbols.
Shadows crawled across the stone like living things, warping and shifting as if reacting to their presence.
Crimson light seeped in through tall, narrow windows lining the walls, bathing everything in an eerie red glow.
The air itself felt heavy.
Oppressive.
"This place is..." Emilia swallowed, her face paling slightly.
"Creepy."
Leon didn’t respond.
He simply stepped forward, eyes scanning the surroundings, senses sharpened.
The [Hell] difficulty wasn’t going to ease them in.
They advanced deeper into the cathedral, their footsteps echoing faintly against the stone floor.
The silence was unsettling.
And then—
Fwish!
A sphere of crimson light shot straight toward them.
"Move!" Leon barked.
They both dodged instinctively.
BOOM!
The orb slammed into the ground where they had been standing, erupting in a violent explosion that shook the entire area around them.
"What the hell?!" Emilia lifted her scepter instantly.
Before either of them could speak again, more crimson orbs began forming in the darkness ahead.
Figures emerged alongside them.
[Moon Sect Devout]
[Level: 25]
[Exclusive Talent: Blood Moon Worshipper (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 30,000]
[Details: Devouts of the "Blood Moon" sect, currently searching for the force hidden deep within the cathedral.]
Emilia’s eyes widened.
"All of them have thirty thousand combat power?!" she exclaimed.
"Holy hell... even I couldn’t beat one of these by myself!"
"They can’t hurt you," Leon said calmly as he took his stance.
"And for me..."
His grip tightened around his sword.
"They’re weak."
Fwish!
Leon activated [Vision Enhancement], his perception sharpening instantly.
At the same time, [Darkness Barrier] enveloped his body in a thin, shifting veil of black energy.
The devouts raised their scepters in unison, crimson energy gathering at their tips.
Leon moved first.
Slash!
He cut through the incoming orbs with precise swings, the explosions dispersing harmlessly as their cores were destroyed mid-air.
In the next instant, Leon raised his staff.
Storm of Lightning!
A violent storm erupted above the devouts, bolts of lightning crashing down relentlessly.
The moment the lightning struck, all of them stiffened, their bodies locking up as electricity coursed through them.
"Now!" Leon shouted.
Spectral Flames!
Emilia’s magic surged forward, ghostly flames engulfing the stunned devouts.
They didn’t even have time to scream.
The combined assault wiped them out instantly.
Ding!
[You have killed x7 "Moon Sect Devout" and gained 14,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 18!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes and 100 free points to distribute.]
Leon felt a surge of power flow through his body.
Emilia did as well, her expression lighting up as she felt her own strength increase.
"Nice," Leon said with a grin.
"Since the enemies here are far above our level, we’ll level up fast."
Emilia nodded eagerly.
"This place is dangerous... but it’s perfect for growth."
Leon quickly checked the drops.
[Moon Sect Devout Robe x7 (Uncommon): +300 Defense, +150 Constitution, +100 Spirit.
Requirement: 1,500 Spirit.]
[Moon Sect Scepter x7 (Rare): +500 Magic Attack, +400 Spirit, +200 Agility.
Requirement: 1,000 Spirit.]
Without hesitation, Leon began fusing them.
Ding!
[You have consumed two identical equipment... enhancement successful!]
He repeated the process until only two items remained: [Moon Sect Devout Robe +3] and [Moon Sect Scepter +2]
Leon handed both to Emilia.
"These are way better than what you’re using," he said.
"Thanks!" Emilia beamed as she equipped them, her stats rising noticeably.
As they continued deeper into the cathedral, Leon spoke again.
"Focus mainly on your [Constitution] and [Spirit].
You don’t need agility if you can tank everything, and strength is pointless for you."
Emilia nodded, "Got it."
They moved forward once more.
More Moon Sect Devouts appeared along the way, but none of them posed a real threat.
Even with 30,000 combat power, they couldn’t break through Leon’s attacks or even approach Emilia.
Still, Leon remained cautious.
This was [Hell] difficulty.
Something worse was coming.
And sure enough, only about ten minutes after entering the cathedral...
Fwish!
Leon spun around just in time to see a dark figure materialize behind Emilia.
A dagger flashed through the air, aimed straight at her back.
Leon didn’t even bother to move even though he saw it though.
’That shoul make more confident in herself,’ he thought.
Because—
Slash!
Clang!
The dagger struck Emilia... and bounced off harmlessly.
The figure froze in confusion.
And before it could react again, Leon rushed forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 67: Rushing Through the Cathedral, The Blood Gate
paragraphs: Upon their arrival in [Universal Ascension], it was completely normal for ordinary players, no matter their race, to know almost nothing about the world they had been thrown into.
There was no guide, no explanation, no long tutorial waiting for them. They were simply dropped in.
Aside from a few basic system messages and vague instructions, the world offered them nothing.
No one explained the rules or how power truly worked.
Everyone was forced to learn through trial, error... and death.
Leon knew this better than anyone.
From his perspective, the difference between players was clear from the very beginning.
Those who came from eternal-level worlds were different. They moved with confidence. They reacted faster.
They were never surprised by sudden changes or hidden mechanics. Even when something completely new appeared, they acted as if they had already expected it.
They knew things. They always did.
Among the countless pieces of information that most players wouldn’t understand until much later, there was one that seemed painfully basic in hindsight: attributes.
Constitution, Strength, Agility and Spirit.
Simple concepts, or so most people believed.
Many players spent weeks, sometimes months, treating attributes as nothing more than numbers.
Things that increased damage or health in a very shallow way. They invested points blindly, copied others, or ignored them entirely while focusing on skills instead.
Only much later did they realize how wrong that approach was. Leon already knew the truth.
After fifteen years inside this world, there was nothing unclear about attributes to him. He understood them far better than most players ever would, even at higher levels.
Take [Constitution], for example.
Most players thought it simply meant how much damage they could take before dying. A bigger health pool. A sturdier body. That was it.
But that understanding was fundamentally flawed. Constitution was not just HP.
It was durability, resistance, how much physical force your body could endure.I
t was how many status effects you could resist or outright ignore.
It was how much punishment you could take without flinching.
A high constitution didn’t just let you survive longer, it changed how the world interacted with you.
The same could be said for [Strength], [Agility], and [Spirit]. They were all deeper than people assumed, though constitution was by far the most misunderstood of them all.
That was why Leon had done something that would have looked reckless to anyone else.
He had let the assassin entity strike Emilia directly. Not because he was careless.
But because he wanted to show her directly.
Fwoosh!
The assassin moved in an instant once more, its figure blurring as it closed the distance. The dagger in its hand shimmered faintly as it slashed toward Emilia with killing intent.
Clang!
The sound rang out sharply as the blade bounced harmlessly off her skin.
There was no blood. No wound. Not even a scratch.
At the exact same moment, Leon moved.
Slash!
His sword cut through the air in a clean arc, forcing the assassin to retreat immediately.
The entity jumped back, landing lightly before taking a stance.
For the first time, Leon and Emilia were able to clearly see it.
[Moon Sect Devout (Mutated)]
[Level: 25]
[Exclusive Talent: Blood Moon Worshipper (B-Level)]
[Combat Power: 35,000]
[Details: A moon sect devout that has decided to take a dagger rather than a scepter.]
This devout was different from the others they had faced so far.
It was stronger. Sharper. More dangerous.
A crimson aura burned within its eyes as it stared at them, its body tense as it surged forward once again.
Slash!
Instead of targeting Leon, it aimed directly for Emilia.
Clang!
Once more, the dagger failed to even pierce her skin.
The devout froze for a split second, disbelief flashing across its twisted expression.
"How...?" it muttered, slashing again and again in desperation. "How is this even possible?!"
No matter how many times it struck, the result was the same. The blade simply could not break through her defense.
"Our turn now," Leon said with a grin.
Powerful Fireball!
A blazing sphere of flame shot forward, roaring through the air. The devout reacted quickly, leaping aside as the fireball exploded where it had been standing.
But the moment it landed—
Divine Beam!
Emilia was already prepared.
A brilliant beam of light shot forward, striking the devout directly before it could regain its balance.
"Argh...!"
The creature screamed as the attack tore through it, its body staggering from the impact.
And before it could even think of counterattacking—
Slash!
Leon appeared behind it. One clean strike was all it took. The devout’s head fell to the ground, its life ending instantly.
Ding!
[You have killed "Moon Sect Devout (Mutated)" and gained 5,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
The devout dropped a [Moon Sect Devout Robe +2], and unlike the others, it also dropped its weapon.
[Moon Sect Dagger (Elite): +500 Attack, +300 Strength, +250 Agility. Requirement: 1,500 Agility.]
Leon glanced at the items briefly before storing them away. His inventory was steadily filling up from all the kills, and he was more than satisfied with the results so far.
Then he turned to Emilia.
"Give me your scepter and robe for a second," Leon said with a grin.
Emilia didn’t hesitate. She already knew exactly what he was planning.
Leon had been saving the items that dropped from the devouts for this exact moment. One by one, he pulled them out and began fusing them together.
Fwoosh! Ding!
[Enhancement failed.]
Leon didn’t stop.
Ding!
[Enhancement successful!]
Again. And again. He continued using the materials he had gathered, pushing the items further and further until—
[Moon Sect Devout Robe +5 (Uncommon): +1,500 Defense, +750 Constitution, +500 Spirit.]
[Moon Sect Scepter +4 (Rare): +1,300 Magic Attack, +1,000 Spirit, +500 Agility.]
Only then did he hand them back to Emilia. Her eyes widened as she looked at the upgraded equipment.
"Holy shit," she muttered. "Your talent really is something..."
"I hope you learned something from what happened earlier," Leon said calmly. "You can’t get hurt."
Emilia still felt some skepticism. She wasn’t the type to blindly believe something like that, and she definitely wasn’t eager to test it herself.
But after seeing a mutated monster fail completely to break through her defense... she couldn’t deny it anymore.
She felt more confident than before. Not enough to throw herself into danger, but enough to trust her own strength.
Just like that, Leon and Emilia continued deeper into the [Hell] difficulty [Blood Moon Cathedral].
Along the way, they encountered new enemies, this time, actual monsters instead of natives.
[Moon Devout Beast]
[Level: 25]
[Combat Power: 34,000]
[Detail: A wolf-like beast that has devoted itself to the "Blood Moon".]
These monsters weren’t much of a threat either, but they served another purpose. They dropped essences.
[Moon Devout Beast: Consuming will increase Spirit by 7 and Constitution by 6.]
Leon consumed them without hesitation, steadily enhancing his attributes even further.
None of the monsters they encountered were strong enough to slow them down, let alone endanger them.
[+105 Spirit, +90 Constitution.]
Thanks to that, Leon continued leveling smoothly.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 19 + 20!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 200 points in all attributes and 200 free points to distribute.]
Emilia glanced around as another group of monsters fell.
"Are you sure this is the [Hell] difficulty?" she joked. "Feels more like easy~"
Leon didn’t answer, but his gaze remained focused ahead.
Before long, they reached the end of the [Blood Moon Cathedral].
And there, it wasn’t a boss that awaited them, but a massive gate engraved with a gigantic crimson symbol.
No matter the direction, all the light of the [Blood Moon] seemed to converge upon it.
The area around the gate was completely silent. No monsters approached. No devouts lingered nearby.
It was as if the place itself was sacred and forbidden.
Even Leon felt something was off.
’That thing doesn’t exist in [Normal] or [Hard] difficulty,’ he thought, his eyes narrowing. ’It really is exclusive to the hardest one.’
Without hesitation, he pulled the [Blood Moon Crystal] from his inventory.
The moment it appeared—
Fwoosh!
The crystal began to float, drifting forward until it stopped directly in front of the gate.
Ding!
[You have been recognized as worthy, Celestial.]
[But unfortunately, you may only proceed alone in the "Blood Heart Challenge"]
"Seriously?"

chapters.title: Chapter 68: Blood Heart Challenge, Unique Item
paragraphs: [Challenges] were something extremely rare in [Universal Ascension]. Rare enough that most players would never see one in their entire lifetime.
Even in the [Higher Domain], where elites gathered, and in the [Eternal Domain], where monsters walked among legends, challenges were still spoken of more like myths.
Some people doubted they even existed. Others believed they were reserved only for those favored directly by the system.
And just as rare as they were... They were terrifyingly difficult.
Every [Challenge] came with strict rules, brutal conditions, and consequences that could permanently lock players out if they failed.
Many didn’t just test strength, they tested awareness, judgment, and understanding of the world.
This was Leon’s first challenge since his rebirth. And he had no intention of losing.
Fwoosh!
The moment the system acknowledged the [Blood Moon Crystal] and judged him worthy, the massive gate before him reacted.
The crimson symbol carved into its surface pulsed once, then cracked apart as the stone doors slowly began to open.
What lay beyond wasn’t a dark corridor. Nor was it another narrow chamber filled with traps.
Instead, Leon found himself staring into something completely different. Beyond the gate was a sanctuary.
Bright vegetation covered the ground, strange plants glowing faintly under the crimson light.
Vines wrapped around white stone structures, and the air itself felt heavy, saturated with power.
In the center of the sanctuary stood a monument, ancient, weathered, and unmistakably important.
Above it all, the sky was dark.
The [Blood Moon] hung directly overhead, positioned perfectly above the monument, as if the entire space had been built around that exact alignment.
Its crimson light poured down, bathing the sanctuary and focusing entirely on the structure below.
Leon paused at the threshold.
"Can you stay back?" he asked, glancing over his shoulder. "I don’t think I can take you with me."
Emilia smiled easily.
"It’s fine," she said, unfazed. "I’ll take the time to level up too."
Leon nodded, "Thanks."
With that, he stepped forward.
The moment his foot crossed the boundary—
Ding!
[You have entered the "Blood Heart Challenge"]
[Challenge: Defend the "Blood Heart" from the monster tide. Do not allow it to be destroyed.]
[If destroyed, it will kill you as well as stop you from ever attempting this challenge again.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
"Hm."
Tolkien had mentioned this challenge.
According to him, the [Moon Sect] had attempted it countless times over the years, and failed every single time.
No matter how many elites they sent, no matter how well they prepared, none of them had succeeded.
That alone told Leon everything he needed to know. This challenge was no joke.
Still, he moved forward.
The instant his entire body entered the sanctuary, the gate behind him shut with a heavy boom, sealing itself completely.
’...Can’t go back, I guess.’
Leon didn’t panic. Instead, he studied his surroundings carefully.
The sanctuary was circular, its edges defined by four tall marble pillars that held up a domed structure.
Each pillar was etched with ancient carvings, worn down by time but still faintly visible.
Whatever this place was, it had existed long before players ever arrived in this world.
At the center stood a pedestal. And on top of it... A heart.
A massive crimson heart, pulsing slowly, rhythmically.
Each beat sent waves of red light outward, absorbing the glow of the [Blood Moon] above.
Thick chains extended from it, binding it to the four pillars, as if preventing it from escaping, or being taken.
No matter what anyone did, those chains couldn’t be broken. Leon knew that already.
To claim it, you had to pass the challenge. He stepped closer and activated [Appraisal].
[Blood Heart (Unique): Holds the power of the "Blood Moon" within it. May be extremely useful to whoever possesses it.]
That was all the system showed him. But Leon didn’t need more.
The moment he saw the word "Unique," his decision was already made.
Unique items were absurdly rare in [Universal Ascension]. Each one carried power far beyond normal equipment.
More importantly, they were one-of-a-kind. Once claimed, they were gone forever.
In his past life, Leon had seen players rise to unimaginable heights simply because they had acquired a single unique item early on.
This heart... He needed it.
Leon tightened his grip on his sword and staff.
And then—
Ding!
Three beams of crimson light slammed down into different corners of the sanctuary.
The ground trembled as the beams solidified, and from each one, a powerful presence began to emerge.
"Looks like it’s starting," Leon said with a grin, "Guess I just need to protect the [Blood Heart] no matter what."
His eyes sharpened as the monsters fully revealed themselves.
[Rotten Moon Devout (Mutated)]
[Level: 25]
[Combat Power: 39,000]
[Details: A moon sect devout that has rotten in this sanctuary for far too long.]
[Blood Archer (Mutated)]
[Level: 25]
[Combat Power: 40,000]
[Details: An archer that forms arrows out of blood, extremely powerful.]
[Blood Bear (Mutated)]
[Level: 25]
[Combat Power: 41,000]
[Details: A bear that had its body completely changed by the power of the blood moon.]
All three were mutated. All three were strong.
And all three appeared from different positions around the sanctuary.
Leon clicked his tongue.
’No wonder this is a challenge.’
The [Blood Bear] moved first, charging forward with terrifying speed, its massive claws gleaming under the crimson light.
Leon prepared to intercept—
Fwoosh!
But before he could move, the [Blood Archer] had already drawn its bow. A blood-red arrow condensed instantly and was released without hesitation.
BAM!
The arrow struck the [Blood Heart] directly. A small crack formed on its surface.
Leon’s eyes widened slightly. Thankfully, the heart wasn’t destroyed.
But now he understood.
’I see...’
His expression darkened.
’Two close-range monsters to force engagement... and one long-range attacker targeting the heart directly.’
Since the challenge had to be completed alone, managing all three simultaneously was brutal. Any moment of hesitation meant another arrow.
This setup would overwhelm almost anyone... but Leon wasn’t anyonre.
Because unlike most others, he could use both a sword and magic!
Leon moved.
Storm of Lightning!
A violent surge of lightning erupted outward, striking all three monsters at once.
Electricity danced across the sanctuary, momentarily disrupting their movements.
Powerful Fireball!
A blazing fireball followed immediately, slamming into the [Blood Archer]. The explosion scorched its body, interrupting its aim and forcing it back.
But in that same instant—
The [Blood Bear] and [Rotten Moon Devout] closed the distance.
Claws and blade came down at the same time.
Leon blocked, deflected, and twisted aside, his expression tightening.
’They’re buying time...’ His eyes flicked toward the archer, ’They’re creating openings for it to fire again.’
It was a coordinated assault. But they had miscalculated.
After deflecting both attacks, he leaped backward, creating space, then turned in one smooth motion.
Crescent Slash!
Fwoosh!
A crescent-shaped blade of energy tore through the air, slicing straight toward the [Blood Archer]. It cut through its body effortlessly, splitting it in half.
The archer collapsed without even making a sound. Silence fell.
Leon turned slowly toward the remaining two monsters, a wide grin spreading across his face.
The [Blood Bear] and [Rotten Moon Devout] glanced at each other. They swallowed.
It didn’t matter. Leon closed the distance and ended them both swiftly.
Their heads hit the ground moments later.
"Phew," Leon exhaled, "I guess it’s no wonder nobody could complete it."
Ding!
[You have killed "Blood Bear" and gained 8,000 experience points.]
[You have killed "Rotten Moon Devout" and gained 7,700 experience points.]
[You have killed "Blood Archer" and gained 7,900 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
He would have ended it there. If it actually was the end.
But suddenly, the [Blood Moon] above reacted. Its light intensified, pulsing violently, as if something had finally noticed him.
Ding!
[The "Blood Moon" does not like your presence. It will send its strongest foe.]
Leon’s grin vanished.
"Oh shit."
BOOM!
A massive crimson beam erupted from the sky, easily ten times larger than the previous ones.
The ground shook violently as something enormous began to descend.
ROOOOAR!
[The "Blood Wyvern" has appeared.]

Rare enough that most players would never see one in their entire lifetime.
Even in the [Higher Domain], where elites gathered, and in the [Eternal Domain], where monsters walked among legends, challenges were still spoken of more like myths.
Some people doubted they even existed.
Others believed they were reserved only for those favored directly by the system.
And just as rare as they were...
They were terrifyingly difficult.
Every [Challenge] came with strict rules, brutal conditions, and consequences that could permanently lock players out if they failed.
Many didn’t just test strength, they tested awareness, judgment, and understanding of the world.
This was Leon’s first challenge since his rebirth.
And he had no intention of losing.
Fwoosh!
The moment the system acknowledged the [Blood Moon Crystal] and judged him worthy, the massive gate before him reacted.
The crimson symbol carved into its surface pulsed once, then cracked apart as the stone doors slowly began to open.
What lay beyond wasn’t a dark corridor.
Nor was it another narrow chamber filled with traps.
Instead, Leon found himself staring into something completely different.
Beyond the gate was a sanctuary.
Bright vegetation covered the ground, strange plants glowing faintly under the crimson light.
Vines wrapped around white stone structures, and the air itself felt heavy, saturated with power.
In the center of the sanctuary stood a monument, ancient, weathered, and unmistakably important.
Above it all, the sky was dark.
The [Blood Moon] hung directly overhead, positioned perfectly above the monument, as if the entire space had been built around that exact alignment.
Its crimson light poured down, bathing the sanctuary and focusing entirely on the structure below.
Leon paused at the threshold.

[If destroyed, it will kill you as well as stop you from ever attempting this challenge again.]

No matter how many elites they sent, no matter how well they prepared, none of them had succeeded.
That alone told Leon everything he needed to know.
This challenge was no joke.

A heart.

More importantly, they were one-of-a-kind.

He needed it.

chapters.title: Chapter 69: The Blood Wyvern, Unshaken Passive
paragraphs: ROOOAR!
The roar shook the entire sanctuary, sending vibrations through the ground and into Leon’s chest.
The creature before him was massive, standing nearly five meters tall. Its body was covered in thick crimson scales that reflected the light of the [Blood Moon], making it impossible to look away.
Wide wings folded behind its back, sharp claws dug into the stone floor, and its presence alone carried overwhelming pressure.
Leon did not hesitate.
Appraisal!
[Blood Wyvern (Challenge Boss)]
[Level: 25]
[Talent: Blood Affinity (B-Level)]
[Combat Power: 50,000]
[Details: A wyvern with a deep affinity to the "Blood Moon".]
"A wyvern this early?" Leon muttered, genuine surprise flashing across his face. "And fifty thousand combat power?"
That was far beyond what he had expected.
Wyverns were not ordinary monsters. While they were weaker than true dragons or drakes, they were still classified as dragon-type creatures.
Fighting one was never simple, especially not at this stage.
Leon had always believed that wyverns only began appearing properly in the [Higher Domain].
He had never once heard of one existing in the [Lower Domain]. Dragons themselves were completely absent here, and even in the [Higher Domain], only a single one was known to exist.
The [Eternal Domain] was where the true nightmares resided. That was where the most terrifying beasts waited.
By the time he reached that place again, Leon knew he would be strong enough to face them. He would have to be.
If he wanted to challenge the gods themselves one day, then creatures like this were only stepping stones.
The memory of the [God of Eternity] surfaced briefly in his mind. Even now, Leon could not imagine a clear way to defeat such an existence.
Still, he knew one thing for certain. It was possible.
ROOOAR!
The [Blood Wyvern] took a heavy step forward, its claws scraping against the stone.
Then its eyes began to glow.
Wyvern Glare!
A dense crimson aura poured out from its gaze, locking directly onto Leon. The pressure was suffocating, aimed not at his body but at his very soul.
Leon grimaced slightly.
He knew this ability well. Several high-tier monsters possessed something similar.
Wyvern Glare imposed a powerful debuff that reduced the enemy’s combat power by twenty percent. Against an opponent this strong, such a debuff could easily decide the outcome of the battle.
With the wyvern’s already absurd combat power, this was meant to make the fight completely one-sided.
But nothing happened. Leon stood still, unaffected.
And...
Ding!
[A "Celestial" cannot be affected by such effects.]
[You have learned the passive skill "Unshaken" linked to your "Celestial" title.]
Leon blinked.
"Oh?
[Unshaken: No matter what happens, you will never feel fear or intimidation when facing enemies. All intimidation-based and fear-based debuffs are nullified.]
Leon had not expected that.
He already knew his [Celestial] title was powerful, but gaining new passives from it was something he had not considered.
"Interesting," he muttered quietly.
If this title could still evolve or unlock abilities, then its potential was even greater than he thought. He quickly refocused.
The [Blood Wyvern] did not seem to care that its glare had failed. It opened its jaws, crimson energy gathering deep within its throat.
Blood Flames!
The temperature in the sanctuary spiked instantly as violent heat rolled outward. Leon’s expression hardened.
The problem was not dodging the attack. The problem was that the wyvern was aiming at both him and the [Blood Heart].
If that attack landed on the heart, it could shatter.
And if the heart broke, the challenge would end instantly. With his death.
"How are you even supposed to stop that?" Leon muttered under his breath.
Now he truly understood why nobody had completed this challenge.

Even if someone was strong enough to fight the monsters, the constant pressure of protecting the heart made everything exponentially harder. The [Moon Sect] must have reached this point before. And failed.
Still, Leon smiled.
"You tried to weaken me first," he said as he rushed forward. "Now it’s my turn."
Fwish! Slash!
Leon swung his sword, striking the wyvern’s scales. The creature blocked the attack with one claw, sparks flying from the impact.
But the wyvern did not stop charging its flames. Leon grinned wider. Because at that exact moment.
Fwoosh!
[Celestial’s Might has activated!]
Leon’s eyes turned silvery white as overwhelming pressure erupted from his body. The air itself seemed to tremble as that pressure crashed directly into the [Blood Wyvern].
Unlike Leon, the wyvern was not immune. The massive creature let out a pained roar as its body stiffened.
Leon had begun to notice a pattern with [Celestial’s Might]. It did not activate against weak enemies, or even moderately strong ones.
It activated only against beings of extreme power.
The [Undead King]. The guardian tied to the [Core of Poison]. And now this wyvern.
"It isn’t just luck," Leon thought as he felt the pressure subside. "It triggers against true threats."
The wyvern’s combat power dropped instantly.
[Blood Wyvern]
[Combat Power: 35,000]
A thirty percent reduction. And more importantly, its [Blood Flames] charge was disrupted.
Leon exhaled slowly. Even so, he did not relax.
Combat power was not everything. The wyvern still had experience, instincts, and deadly skills. Even at reduced strength, it could easily kill someone careless.
ROOOAR!
The wyvern roared again and immediately began charging its flames once more.
Leon clenched his teeth. It was intelligent.
It understood that Leon would die the moment the [Blood Heart] was destroyed.
"I need to kill it before that happens," Leon said quietly.
He charged forward again, staff and sword moving together.
Powerful Fireball! Storm of Lightning! Crescent Slash!
A barrage of attacks slammed into the wyvern. Flames exploded against its body, lightning wrapped around its scales, and the crescent slash carved across its chest.
The wyvern staggered slightly. But it did not fall. Its scales were too thick. Too resilient.
The damage was real, but not decisive. Leon’s eyes narrowed.
"If Emilia were here," he mumbled, "her buffs would make this much easier."
Her [Strength Buff] and [Speed Buff] could have shifted the fight instantly.
But Leon did not allow himself to dwell on that.
If he wanted to advance further in this world, he needed to be able to handle battles like this alone.
Vision Enhancement! Darkness Barrier!
His perception sharpened as shadows wrapped around his body. Leon rushed forward again, blade flashing.
Slash! Slash!
The wyvern retaliated fiercely, claws and tail crashing down. Sparks flew as blade met scale. The air rang with every collision.
The exchange was brutal and relentless. And then...
SLASH!
Leon found an opening.
His sword carved cleanly through one of the wyvern’s arms. Blood sprayed across the sanctuary as the limb fell to the ground.
The wyvern screamed in fury. Leon did not stop.
Shadow Slash!
His body dissolved into darkness, vanishing from sight as he moved to strike from the shadows.
Normally, this would have ended the fight. But this time, Leon made a mistake.
The wyvern did not stop charging its attack even as Leon cut off its arm and disappeared. In fact, it accelerated.
The creature opened its jaws wide, eyes locking directly onto the [Blood Heart].
Blood Flames!
Crimson fire erupted forward in a violent torrent.
"Oh shit!"
Leon’s eyes widened. His shadow-infused strike sliced through the wyvern’s head, killing it instantly.
But it was too late. The flames had already been released.
They struck the [Blood Heart] for a brief moment.
And then...
Ding!
[The "Blood Heart" is in critical condition. Defend it no matter what!]
Leon’s face darkened. He did not hesitate.
He rushed forward with everything he had left, knowing that if he failed now, he would die anyway.

chapters.title: Chapter 70: Acquiring The Blood Heart, 150 Reputation Points
paragraphs: Leon still had his [Darkness Barrier] active.
It was being continuously fueled by his [Embodiment of Darkness] sub-talent, which meant that even at only level 2, the barrier was absurdly strong.
At this stage, it was powerful enough to block nearly any attack that tried to pierce through it.
Because of that, Leon made a decision instantly. The moment he realized the [Blood Flames] would hit the [Blood Heart], he moved.
Fwoosh!
In a blink, Leon placed himself directly in front of the heart. The torrent of crimson flames slammed into him instead.
Anyone else who tried something like this would have either had their barrier shattered instantly or would have been burned alive by the overwhelming heat.
Even high-level players would hesitate before doing something so reckless.
His [Darkness Barrier] flared violently as it absorbed the impact.
Cracks spread across its surface, spiderwebbing outward under the pressure of the flames.
The heat was intense enough to warp the air itself. And yet, Leon stood firm.
The flames hit his barrier and were pushed aside, spreading harmlessly to the left and right. They no longer touched the [Blood Heart] behind him.
Seconds passed. The pressure continued.
Leon clenched his teeth as his darkness barrier drained rapidly, but he held his position.
Finally, the [Blood Flames] faded away completely. Silence returned to the sanctuary.
Leon slowly turned his head and looked behind him. The [Blood Heart] was still there.
Several deep cracks ran across its surface, glowing faintly with crimson light, but it had not shattered. It was still intact.
Leon exhaled deeply. And then...
Ding!
[You have completed the "Blood Heart" Challenge.]
"Perfect," Leon muttered, a wide grin spreading across his face.
Only then did he allow himself to relax.
He straightened his posture and looked around as more system panels appeared before him, triggered by the death of the [Blood Wyvern].
Ding!
[You have killed "Blood Wyvern (Challenge Boss)" and gained 12,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered. Items have been automatically placed in your storage space.]
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 21!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 100 points in all attributes and 100 free points to distribute.]
"Haha!" Leon laughed out loud. The surge of power felt satisfying.
His [Storage Space] was now packed with loot from the three mutated monsters as well as the [Blood Wyvern]. Even without checking, he knew the drops would be excellent.
Still, before looking at any of that, Leon turned back toward the pedestal. The [Blood Heart] began to glow.
Its crimson light intensified, spreading outward in gentle pulses that sent small shockwaves through the sanctuary.
The air trembled slightly as the heart responded to the completed challenge.
Clang!
One of the chains binding it to the pedestal shattered.
Clang! Clang!
The remaining chains broke one after another, fragments falling to the ground and dissolving into particles of light.
Slowly, the [Blood Heart] lifted into the air. It hovered above the pedestal, rotating slowly, as if examining Leon in return.
Ding!
[The "Blood Heart" has recognized you as its true owner.]
Leon’s eyes widened. Before he could react, the heart shot forward. Straight into his chest.
A warm, powerful sensation flooded through his body. His heartbeat synced with the pulsing rhythm of the heart, as if it had always belonged there.
Leon stiffened for a brief moment, then relaxed as the sensation settled.
Items that fused directly with a player’s body were extraordinarily rare. Unlike equipment or consumables, they never entered the [Storage Space].
They became part of the user. And more importantly, they could never be stolen.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have obtained the "Blood Heart" (Unique Special Item).]
Leon immediately appraised it again. Now that it had fully bonded with him, more information appeared.
[Blood Heart (Unique Special Item): Contains the holy power of the "Blood Moon", allowing its user to bless a piece of their equipment.]
[Once used, the blessing will only reset after killing a certain number of monsters.]
[The monsters must not be significantly weaker than the user.]
[Each piece of equipment can only be blessed once. The "Blood Heart" itself can be used infinitely.]

Even in his past life, Leon had never possessed an item like this.
A unique item that could permanently bless equipment was beyond rare. It was the kind of item that could completely change a player’s growth path.
And unlike equipment that could be dropped or stolen upon death, the [Blood Heart] was untouchable.
If Leon died permanently with it, no one else would ever be able to obtain it.
The moment that thought crossed his mind, another system notification echoed across the entire [Lower Domain].
Ding!
[Player "Celestial" is the first to complete the "Blood Heart Challenge" and has been rewarded with 50 Reputation Points.]
Ding!
[Your reputation has reached 150, you will now gain an additional 25 attribute points per level.]
"DAMN!"

Global announcements were rare, especially in the [Lower Domain]. The fact that this one had triggered meant that truly no one even came close to clearing it.
And that meant every single player in the [Lower Domain] saw his name. Including those at level 50.
Leon didn’t know what to think of the new attention, as it could indeed be dangerous.
Many level 50 players would possibly instantly try to catch him to see if they could "steal" what he had.
Though for now, they were unaware of where the [Blood Heart Challenge] was.
And by the time those "killer players" at the top attempted to find him, he would already be out of [Moon City] hopefully.
"What the hell is the Blood Heart Challenge?"
"Celestial? Never heard of him before."
"Wait, isn’t that the guy selling crazy stuff in the Trading House?"
The discussions erupted instantly. Players across cities and zones stopped what they were doing, trying to understand what had just happened.
The last global announcement had been a long time ago, and seeing a new one immediately drew attention.
Meanwhile, Emilia, who was still inside of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] right outside the sanctuary, saw the announcement and laughed softly after firing a [Divine Beam] at an enemy.
"Haha, I knew he’d beat it," she said with a grin.
She had spent the few minutes he spent in the sanctuary killing monsters.
Since none of them could harm her, it made it much easier to kill them one by one with her skills.

Base attributes, Heaven’s Blessing, and now reputation bonuses all stacked together. That kind of growth was terrifying.
Most players in the [Lower Domain] never even reached 150 reputation points. Gaining reputation required doing things considered extraordinary by the system.
Leon had surpassed that without even reaching level 25.
"Alright," Leon said quietly. "First things first."
He opened his [Storage Space].
"Let’s see what I got."
Fwoosh!
The interface expanded before him, filled with new items and materials, each one waiting to be examined.
After that, he planned to test the [Blood Heart] blessing. He wanted to see just how powerful it truly was.

chapters.title: Chapter 71: B-Level Blood Affinity, Blessing An Item
paragraphs: Leon went through the items one by one, his gaze steady as each panel appeared before him.
[Blood Bear Essence: Consuming will increase Constitution by 8 and Strength by 7.]
[Blood Bear Claw (Epic Material)]
[Blood Bear Fur (Epic Material)]
[Rotten Devout Dagger (Elite): +600 Attack, +350 Strength, +270 Agility. Requirement: Level 25]
[Rotten Devout Robe (Epic): +800 Defense, +400 Spirit, +400 Strength, +250 Agility. Makes users immune to "Decay" and "Weakness". Requirement: Level 25.]
[Rotten Potion (Legendary): Drink this to be affected by "Weakness"]
[Blood Archer Essence: Consuming will increase Agility by 12.]
These were the rewards from the first three mutated monsters he had killed inside the challenge.
They were good items, solid, valuable, and useful, but none of them truly caught Leon’s attention.
He had seen similar things before. Without hesitation, he consumed the two essences.
Warmth flowed through his body twice in succession, his Constitution, Strength, and Agility quietly increasing as the system confirmed the gains.
The rest of the materials and equipment were sent back into his [Storage Space] without another thought.
He could sell them later. Then, his focus shifted to the last batch of drops.
The items from the [Blood Wyvern]. This was the real prize.
[Skill Stones x7]
[Enhancement Stones x5]
[Blood Wyvern Essence: Consuming will increase all stats by 10.]
[Blood Wyvern Armor (Legendary): +1,500 Defense, +700 Constitution, +500 Spirit, +250 Agility. Prevents "Bleeding". Requirement: Blood-related sub-talent or skill.]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Blood Affinity (B-Level)]
"...Damn."
Leon couldn’t help but let the word slip out.
This was a ridiculous haul.

Even for a challenge boss, these rewards were generous to the point of absurdity. Any one of these items would make waves if placed in the [Trading House], especially the armor and the sub-talent scroll.
As usual, Leon didn’t waste time. He consumed the [Blood Wyvern Essence] immediately.
The effect was far stronger than the previous ones.
A surge of power rushed through his limbs, his mana core pulsing as every single attribute climbed upward at once.
His body adjusted quickly, the system stabilizing the increase without any backlash.
Once that was done, his eyes moved to the final item. The scroll. A blood-type sub-talent.
Leon frowned slightly.
’Blood-type...?’
It wasn’t that he disliked it. It was more that he didn’t see an immediate use for it. Blood-related abilities were niche, and most players avoided them unless they had a specific build in mind.
Selling it wouldn’t fetch much either. Even as a B-Level sub-talent, demand for blood affinity was low.
Still, Leon wasn’t the kind of person to hoard unused power.
And besides, the armor. His gaze shifted back to the [Blood Wyvern Armor].
It was leagues above what he was currently wearing. Leon exhaled and made his decision.
Fwoosh!
Mana flowed into the scroll as he tore it open. The parchment dissolved into crimson light, which rushed straight into his body, merging with his essence.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have learned the B-Level Sub-Talent: "Blood Affinity"]
[Blood Affinity (B-Level): Your affinity with blood is beyond everyone else’, allowing you to have better control of it.]
The description was vague. Almost annoyingly so.
Leon glanced at it for a moment, then shrugged. He’d figure it out later.
Right now, he had something better to do.
He unequipped his [Dark Sentinel Armor +4 (Rare)], the familiar weight lifting off his shoulders, and immediately equipped the new armor.
The moment the [Blood Wyvern Armor] settled over his body, Leon felt the difference.
"Phew..."
The armor was heavier, sturdier, and carried a faint pressure of its own. It felt alive in a way, resilient, dense, and perfectly suited to absorb punishment.
Bleeding immunity alone made it worth the switch.
With that, Leon had checked every single drop from the [Blood Heart Challenge].
Everything except one thing. The most important thing. His gaze sharpened.
"The [Blood Heart]."
The unique special item bound directly to his body.
According to its description, he could bless a piece of equipment.
The concept of [Blessing] was unknown to him though, which meant... He was about to find out firsthand.
Leon reached into his [Storage Space] and pulled out his weapon of choice. The [Void Staff].
It was his strongest piece of equipment. The core of his build.
If anything deserved the blessing, it was this. Leon closed his eyes and focused inward.
The rhythm of his heartbeat changed, slowly syncing with the steady pulse of the [Blood Heart] embedded in his chest.
A faint warmth spread through him as he reached out, directing its power.
And then—
Ding!
[You have used the "Blood Heart" on the "Void Staff"]
[You have blessed the "Void Staff"]
Fwoosh!
Crimson light erupted around the staff, wrapping it completely. The aura didn’t burn or explode. It flowed.
Like liquid fire, it seeped into the weapon, threading itself along the shaft, sinking deep into the material. The power carved invisible pathways, embedding itself permanently.
When the glow finally faded, faint crimson lines remained etched into the staff, pulsing softly like veins.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He opened the item panel.
[Void Staff +2 (Mythical): +1,500 Spirit.]
[Blood Heart Blessing: The "Spirit" bonus of the staff is tripled.]
Leon froze. He stared at the panel. Then his eyes widened.
"Holy shit."
There was no other reaction possible. Tripled.
His staff alone now granted him an absurd amount of Spirit, far beyond what any player at his level should possess.
And instantly, Leon understood. This was what a [Blessing] meant.
An additional effect layered on top of an item.
It could be anything: raw stats, unique bonuses, special effects, or strange perks. And it depended entirely on the equipment being blessed.
Which meant the [Blood Heart] wasn’t just powerful. It was flexible. Dangerously so.
No wonder it was a unique item. No wonder it required such a brutal challenge. In the right hands, this thing could shape an entire build into something monstrous.
Ding!
[Kill monsters to recharge the "Blood Heart" and be able to bless another piece of equipment.]
Leon clicked his tongue softly. He’d have to kill blindly until it was ready again.
Still, he was more than satisfied. Everything about this challenge had gone perfectly.
The gate that led back to the sanctuary opened once more, signaling that he could return to the [Blood Moon Cathedral].
Leon stepped forward. But just as he was about to leave—
Ding!
[You have cleared the "Blood Heart Challenge" and freed Tolkien from his chains, return to him to complete the quest!]
Leon grinned.
"Right. That [Storage Space Expander] is non-negotiable."
Fwoosh!
He passed through the gate, the scenery shifting instantly.
The moment he returned to the [Blood Moon Cathedral], he stopped.
"...Damn."
The area was a mess. Dozens of corpses littered the ground: monsters, moon sect devouts, shattered remains scorched by magic.
And in the middle of it all, divine beams of light crashed down from Emilia’s scepter. Spectral flames tore through enemies.
Emilia was still fighting.
She moved with excitement, her spells flying freely as she wiped out anything that dared approach.
Leon stepped forward, amused.
"Are you done?" he asked with a grin.
"Hah?!" Emilia spun around, startled. She looked at the destruction around her, then laughed awkwardly. "H-Haha... I might’ve gone a bit overboard. But hey! I’m level 20 now!"
Leon nodded approvingly.
"Good. I’m level 21. Only four levels until my second assessment. You’re five away. We should reach level 25 soon."
"Yay!" Emilia beamed. Then she paused. "Though... we still need to defeat the [Zone Boss]."
"Yeah."
The [Blood Wyvern] had been the challenge boss.
Stronger, more dangerous, but still not the ruler of the zone.
Leon had actually been wondering where the real boss was.
And then—
Fwoosh!
The air trembled.
Crimson light gathered ahead of them, forming a tall figure that radiated authority and pressure.
Leon’s eyes narrowed.
"So that’s it."
The figure stepped forward, robes flowing, eyes wide with shock.
"Y-You..." it spoke, staring at Leon. "You beat the [Blood Heart Challenge]?!"
The [Zone Boss]. The [Blood Moon Saint].
A high-ranking member of the [Moon Sect], and the strongest among them.
"H-How is this even possible..."
Leon’s grin widened. He didn’t answer. He was already planning how fast he would bring it down.

chapters.title: Chapter 72: Blood Moon Saint, Blood Beam Skill
paragraphs: Leon’s gaze locked onto the panel floating before him.
[Blood Moon Saint (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 25]
[Exclusive Talent: Blood Moon Worshipper (A-Level)]
[Talent: Blood Affinity (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 42,000]
[Details: The saint of the "Moon Sect" in "Moon City", able to condense the power of the blood moon perfectly.]
The pressure rolling off the figure was real.
Even standing several meters away, Leon could feel the faint pull of blood mana in the air, as if the entire cathedral was responding to the saint’s presence.
The man floated slightly above the ground, robes dyed crimson, symbols of the [Moon Sect] glowing faintly across his body.
His eyes shone like twin blood moons as he stared directly at Leon.
"The [God of the Moon] is not pleased with your interferences," the Blood Moon Saint said coldly. "You have disrupted what should never have been touched. We shall get rid of you once and for all."
Leon didn’t answer. He simply raised his staff and pointed it forward, a grin spreading across his face.
That reaction made the saint’s expression darken.

"You have no idea what you have just done, child," the saint continued, his voice echoing through the cathedral. "Do you truly believe the [Moon Sect] exists only in the [Lower Domain]? We have many more partners in—"
He never finished the sentence. Leon didn’t let him.
Power surged through Leon’s body as mana poured into his staff.
Powerful Fireball!
The words were calm. Casual.
And yet—
Fire began to condense at the tip of the [Void Staff], twisting violently as the surrounding air warped under the pressure.
The mana density climbed instantly, far beyond what should have been possible for a level 21 player.
The fireball expanded, growing larger and hotter by the second, its surface swirling like molten lava.
The Blood Moon Saint’s eyes widened.
"S-Such power..." he muttered. "HOW?!"
Even Leon knew it made no sense. At least, not normally.
No one at this level should be able to cast magic with this level of destructive force.
But Leon wasn’t "normal" anymore. The answer was simple: the [Blood Heart].
More specifically, the blessing placed on the [Void Staff].
By tripling the staff’s Spirit bonus, it had pushed Leon’s magic potential into an absurd range.
His panel told the story clearly:
Nearly ten thousand Spirit. At this stage of [Eternal Ascension], that number was outright monstrous.
Even some level 35 players would struggle against it.
With stats like that, Leon’s spells didn’t just hit hard. They erased things.
"S-Shit...!" the Blood Moon Saint shouted.
"Blood Barrier!
Crimson light exploded outward as the saint desperately summoned his defensive skill, layers of blood mana stacking together to form a thick barrier in front of him.
Normally, it would have been more than enough, but this wasn’t a normal spell.
The fireball didn’t slow down. It pierced straight through the barrier like it wasn’t even there.
BOOM!
The explosion engulfed the saint completely.
Flames roared outward, scorching the cathedral floor, cracking the stone beneath them. The intense heat incinerated everything in its path.
When the flames faded, nothing remained.
The Blood Moon Saint was dead. Silence filled the cathedral.
"...Wow," Emilia muttered, staring at the scorched ground. "You grew several times stronger in just a few minutes?!"
Leon lowered his staff, exhaling slowly.
"Unique special item," he said with a grin. "Depending on how long it takes to recharge the [Blood Heart], I’ll probably use it on one of your strongest items too."
Emilia blinked, then smiled.
"That thing is terrifying."
Leon nodded. Of course, there was a limit.
If the [Blood Heart] required thousands upon thousands of monster kills to recharge, he’d have to prioritize his own equipment first.
Still, Leon wasn’t worried.
There were many ways to make his allies stronger: methods far beyond simple equipment bonuses. This was only one of them.
Ding!
[You have killed "Blood Moon Saint (Zone Boss)" and gained 8,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
Unfortunately, Emilia didn’t receive any experience from the kill.
Leon’s fireball had ended the fight too quickly. But it didn’t matter.
At her current strength, grinding to level 25 alone wouldn’t be difficult anymore.
Leon turned his attention to the loot.
[Blood Scepter (Legendary): +800 Magic Attack, +600 Spirit, +200 Agility. Requirement: Blood-related skill or sub-talent.]
[Skill Book: Blood Beam (Legendary)]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Blood Affinity (C-Level)]
[Skill Stones x4]
"Pretty good."
The [Blood Scepter] was undeniably powerful, but Emilia’s current weapon was already at its maximum level, making it slightly better overall.
The sub-talent scroll wasn’t particularly useful to Leon either, since he already possessed a higher-level version.
That left one thing. The skill book.
Leon’s eyes narrowed as he opened its description.
[Blood Beam (Legendary): Focus the power of your blood affinity before firing a concentrated beam at your enemies, may cause "Bleeding". Requirement: Blood Affinity (C-Level) or above.]
"Oh?
A new spell was always welcome. Especially now.
With his Spirit stat reaching absurd heights, any magic-based skill he learned would scale into something terrifying.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He pulled the skill book from his [Storage Space] and poured mana into it.
The book dissolved into red light that flowed straight into his body.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Blood Beam"]
Leon clenched his fist slightly.
’This will be useful,’ he thought. ’Especially with the second assessment coming soon.’
Assessments were no joke. The second one, at level 25, was where many players failed to progress and get stronger.
The third, at level 50, separated normal players from the strongest before entering the [Higher Domain].
Leon intended to pass them all at their strongest difficulty. Then he glanced at his panel.
[Free Points to Allocate: 400]
"...Damn."
Anyone who saw this amount of free points not allocated would probably curse at Leon, but he didn’t mind much.
He already knew exactly what he wanted.
"All into Spirit."
Fwoosh!
The points vanished instantly.
His Spirit stat jumped by another 400, pushing it fully past the 10,000 mark.
This was a growth beyond what anybody could achieve without either luck, information or... being from an eternal-level world.
The [Blood Heart] had proven its worth beyond doubt. And Leon knew this was only the beginning, as there were surely other unique special items to grab.
Also, there were stronger enemies out there in [Eternal Ascension].
If he wanted to face them all... this level of power was the minimum.
After everything was settled, the exit portal of the [Blood Moon Cathedral] finally appeared.
A swirling gateway of crimson light.
"Shouldn’t we grind a bit more?" Emilia asked. "We won’t be able to come back here after leaving."
Leon scratched his chin.
"I think we’d run out of monsters eventually," he said. "And I want to complete the quest."
"Alright," Emilia nodded, satisfied.
Together, they stepped toward the portal.
Fwoosh!
The scenery shifted. A few seconds later, they emerged outside the cathedral’s entrance.
Thousands of players were still gathered nearby, busy fighting, trading, or simply watching the massive structure.
No one noticed Leon and Emilia slipping away.
"Let’s leave quietly before the [Moon Sect] arrives," Leon said. "I can beat them, but it’d cause chaos."
Emilia nodded, gripping her scepter.
And just like that, the two headed toward Tolkien’s shop—
Eager to see how the blacksmith was doing now that his chains had finally been broken.

chapters.title: Chapter 73: Tolkien is Free, The Storage Space Expander
paragraphs: Meanwhile, inside Tolkien’s shop, events were unfolding at the exact moment Leon completed the [Blood Heart Challenge].
Tolkien was still bound.
Heavy chains wrapped around his legs, and torso, glowing faintly with restrictive runes that drained his strength nonstop.
They anchored him to the ground and suppressed his power, forcing him to remain in place day and night.
Even breathing felt heavier with those things on him.
For years, the [Moon Sect] had used these chains to keep him under control.
They forced him to work endlessly, crafting weapons, repairing equipment, and most importantly, creating the [Blood Moon Crystals].
Every swing of his hammer was done under threat. They had promised him freedom.
All he had to do was wait until they obtained the [Blood Heart].
But now, that heart was gone. The door of the shop burst open.
Several figures stepped inside at once.
A tall man clad in crimson armor walked forward, his presence alone making the air tense.
Behind him followed dozens of [Moon Sect Devouts], their expressions cold and hostile.
The moon sect general looked directly at Tolkien.
"Alas," the general said calmly, "you have failed."
Tolkien let out a low laugh.
"Hah," he said, lifting his head slightly. "You mean that you failed."
The general’s eyes narrowed.
"Our failure is yours as well," he replied. "For you will die today."
The devouts tightened their grip on their weapons. There was no hesitation in their movements.
They had decided to kill him now that he was no longer useful.

"But do not fret," the general continued, raising his sword slowly. "This is merely a stepping stone in the grand scheme of things. I know you are far stronger than us, but eventually... you will fall."
The blade flashed.
Slash!
The sword cut across Tolkien’s chest, carving a deep wound that sent blood dripping down his torso.
Tolkien grunted but did not scream. He was level 50.
In normal circumstances, none of these people would have even dared to touch him.
But the chains changed everything.
They suppressed his attributes to such an extent that even someone at level 25 could injure him, given enough time.
It would still take a long while to kill him, but it was possible.
The [Moon Sect] thought this was their moment.
Unfortunately for them, they had chosen the worst possible timing.
Ding!
["Celestial" has taken the "Blood Heart" and freed you from your chains.]
Tolkien blinked.
"Oh?" he muttered, lifting his eyebrows in genuine surprise. "That kid actually did it?"
The runes on the chains flickered. Then shattered.
One by one, the restraints disintegrated into dust, their suppressive power vanishing completely.
In a single breath, Tolkien stood up.
The air around him shifted violently as his true presence erupted outward.
"Huh—
The moon sect general barely managed to utter that sound before Tolkien moved.
The hammer in Tolkien’s hand slammed forward with terrifying force. The general’s head exploded on impact.
His body collapsed instantly, lifeless before it even hit the floor. The devouts froze. Their faces went pale.
"W-What...?"
That was all they managed to say. Tolkien did not waste time.
He stepped forward, each movement precise and heavy, his hammer swinging again and again.
Each strike ended a life. None of the devouts could even hope to resist him.
The difference in strength was absolute. In mere seconds, the shop was silent once more.
Bodies littered the floor, blood pooling beneath them. Tolkien exhaled slowly and looked around.
Then he waited. A few minutes passed. Footsteps echoed from outside.
The door opened again. Leon and Emilia stepped inside.
Leon’s eyes swept across the scene, taking in the corpses and the shattered remains of the chains.
"Wow," Leon said calmly. "I guess you really were stronger than expected."
Tolkien snorted.
"Hm. They kept me chained for years," he replied. "That doesn’t mean I got rusty."
Leon nodded, then scratched his chin.
"How did they even capture you in the first place?" he asked. "You’re level 50. That shouldn’t be possible."
Tolkien’s expression darkened. He said nothing.
The silence stretched for a moment. Leon didn’t press further. He had no reason to.
The important part was that the quest was complete, and the outcome had been more than worth it.
Tolkien reached behind the counter and tossed something toward Leon.
"Here," he said. "You earned it."
Leon caught the item easily. It was small, about the size of his palm, shaped like a tiny brown backpack.
The [Storage Space Expander].
Appraisal!
[Storage Space Expander (Mythical): Use to increase "Storage Space" capacity by 30.]
’Nice.’
Leon didn’t hesitate. He poured mana into the item, and it dissolved into light that flowed straight into him.
Ding!
[Your "Storage Space" capacity has reached 140.]
Leon’s eyes lit up.
What made this even better was the fact that it didn’t increase the cost of his next expansion.
The base price remained the same. That alone made this item absurdly valuable.
Another panel appeared immediately after.
Ding!
[Your reputation with "Tolkien, The Cursed Blacksmith" has increased exponentially.]
Leon smiled. Then he appraised Tolkien again.
[Tolkien, The Cursed Blacksmith]
[Level: 50]
[Talent: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
[Details: A blacksmith that has been chained by the "Moon Sect" for a long time, now eager to start making weapons again.]
Leon knew what that meant. Tolkien was one of the strongest natives in the [Lower Domain].
Even level 50 players would struggle against him.
His raw stats were absurd, and that was without considering the skills he possessed.
At Leon’s current level, defeating him would be impossible.
"So," Leon said, breaking the silence, "what now? Are you staying in [Moon City]?"
Tolkien looked around his ruined shop.
For a moment, he said nothing. Then he grinned.
"Heh. I actually like this city," he said. "But my shop is destroyed. I think I’ll relocate."
Leon blinked.
He didn’t question it further. His reputation with Tolkien was already high enough.
He could sell materials to him, request services, and possibly ask for help in the future. That was all that mattered.
Tolkien walked out of the shop. Emilia’s eyes sparkled.
"Do we follow him?" she asked eagerly. "I want to see what he’s planning!"
Leon chuckled.
"Why not," he said. "We can take a break after everything that happened and push to level 25 tomorrow."
"Yay!"
And just like that, Leon and Emilia followed Tolkien through the streets of [Moon City].
Several [Moon Sect Devouts] attempted to block their path. None survived.
Tolkien crushed them effortlessly, barely even slowing down. Leon watched closely.
After about fifteen minutes, they reached the main square of [Moon City], right near the entrance gate.
"Oh, we’re back here," Emilia said, looking around. "Wait... I think I know what he’s about to do!"
Leon raised an eyebrow.
"Hm?"
Tolkien stopped. He turned toward the crowd and grinned.
"Alright," he said loudly. "Let’s get to work."
He pulled wood from his storage space and began assembling a stand.
In just a few minutes, a solid blacksmith stall stood in a busy corner of the square. Then Tolkien shouted.
"I am the best blacksmith there is in the [Lower Domain]! I can repair or enhance your equipment and create new ones for a price!"
Players nearby began to turn their heads.
"A blacksmith?"
"Wait, maybe enhancement success rates are better if he does it."
"I don’t care if I have to pay, I failed my upgrade three times already."
More and more attention gathered around the stand. Leon stared. His eyes widened.
’No way,’ he thought.
Tolkien was setting up shop. Right here. In the middle of [Moon City].
