chapters.title: Chapter 89: Facing The Guardian Dragon of Elements
paragraphs: Most dragons were capable of speech.
They were not mindless beasts, but highly intelligent beings, creatures that could think, analyze, and strategize far better than most players.
Their combat instincts were refined, their experience vast, and their pride immense.
But as had been stated countless times before, there wasn’t a single dragon roaming freely in the [Lower Domains].

Even in the [Higher Domain], the few dragons that existed were treated as walking disasters. Just one of them had managed to slaughter tens of thousands of players by itself before finally being driven away.
So the fact that there was one here, inside an S-Rank assessment, meant only one thing.
This place was guarding something that dragons absolutely did not want anyone to find.

"You should have just left the assessment and taken your reward," the elemental dragon said coldly as it expanded its massive wings. The chamber trembled under the pressure of its presence. "Now you die."
Leon listened calmly. Much like the first assessment, failing here wouldn’t truly kill him.
It would simply count as a failure and force him to proceed to the A-Rank assessment instead.
But even knowing that, this was not something Leon could shrug off lightly.
Failing here would be a devastating loss.
He had fully expected to clear this assessment. More than that, he had expected to gain something incredible from it.
Still... Leon wasn’t shaken by the dragon’s power.
He had entered this place willingly. And if he was being honest with himself, he should have expected a challenge like this. Something far beyond the norm. Something that pushed him to the edge.
And more than anything else, Leon still had [Celestial Might].
On the other hand, the dragon noticed his lack of fear.
"It seems to me that you aren’t bothered by this," the elemental dragon said, its lips curling upward into a cruel grin. "Then I shall show you the difference between our powers."
Dragon Glare!
The dragon opened its eyes fully.
The vertical slits of its pupils glowed intensely, radiating an overwhelming pressure that flooded the entire chamber.
If anyone else had been here, someone around level 30, or even level 40, they would have instantly been struck by [Fear].
Their bodies would freeze, their minds would scream, and their instincts would force them to kneel or flee.
That was the true terror of dragons. Their mere presence was enough to crush the unprepared.
But unfortunately for the dragon—
Unshaken!
Leon’s title passive activated instantly. The oppressive fear vanished as if it had never existed.
"This is..." the dragon muttered, genuine surprise flashing across its expression.
But it didn’t get the time to react. Leon had already raised his staff.
Powerful Fireball! Storm of Lightning!
A massive fireball formed at the tip of Leon’s staff, compressing heat and mana before shooting forward at incredible speed.
At the same time, a violent storm of lightning erupted around the dragon, bolts crashing down relentlessly from every direction.
Boom! Zap!
The attacks collided with the elemental dragon, and did absolutely nothing. Not even a scratch.
"My talent protects me from elemental attacks," the elemental dragon said calmly, a mocking grin spreading across its face. "How unfortunate."
"...Damn."
Leon could feel it. His spells had truly done no damage whatsoever.
Even lightning, an element beyond the four basic ones, was somehow being negated. The dragon’s exclusive talent was far more complete than Leon had initially expected.
Still... That wasn’t all Leon had.
Blood Beam!
Leon focused his power again, mana surging violently through his staff. Using the brief instant while the dragon was mocking him—
BOOM!
A massive beam of crimson energy shot forward, tearing through the air and slamming into the dragon’s body.
This time, it worked. The elemental dragon recoiled slightly as the attack tore into its scales, drawing blood.
[Blood] was an advanced element after all. And that made all the difference.
Still, the damage wasn’t enough to be fatal.
The dragon roared, its voice echoing violently throughout the chamber.
"You insignificant being..."
Elemental Ball!
"...You shall join all the ones who ever stood in our way."
The four elements surged violently around the dragon, converging together. Fire, water, wind, and earth twisted and compressed, forming a massive orb of condensed elemental energy.
Leon stared at the orb, his expression growing serious.
But more than the attack itself, something else bothered him.
’Why the hell didn’t [Celestial Might] activate?’
It always activated against overwhelming foes. Always.
It was meant to give him a fighting chance when facing something far stronger than himself.
And yet, it hadn’t triggered. There was no way such an ability had a random limit.
Which meant, he hadn’t met all the activation conditions.
’I’m clearly facing an overwhelming enemy,’ Leon thought. ’So that’s one condition...’
His eyes narrowed.
’Which means there must be another.’
Leon replayed past fights in his mind. Every time [Celestial Might] had activated. Every detail.
And then—
"Oh," Leon muttered quietly. "I get it."
"DIE!" the dragon roared.
The [Elemental Ball] launched forward, tearing through the chamber with terrifying force. The aura alone was enough to warp the air around it.
If Leon was hit directly, he would be obliterated.
Even Emilia would suffer severe injuries if something like this struck her head-on.
And so—
Shadow Slash!
Leon activated his upgraded ability instantly, his body melting into the shadows.
Thanks to [Shadow Slash] being at level 2, and because of his [Embodiment of Darkness] sub-talent, the concealment effect was vastly stronger than before.
Leon didn’t just disappear. He became one with the darkness.
BOOM!
The elemental ball detonated exactly where Leon had been standing less than half a second earlier, sending shockwaves rippling across the chamber.
"You are not strong enough to face the might of a dragon," the elemental dragon laughed. "But at least I got to test my new ability thanks to you."
The dragon truly believed Leon had died.
As a monster, it didn’t receive notifications when players failed or died. And from its perspective, there was no way someone like Leon could have dodged, or survived, that attack.
And yet—
"You missed."
The voice came from behind it.
Before the dragon could react, Leon appeared directly at its back, his blade already mid-swing and charged with dense darkness.
SLASH!
The strike landed. Ripples of dark energy exploded outward as Leon’s blade carved into the dragon’s neck.
A dragon’s body was terrifyingly durable. Their scales alone could shrug off most attacks. Even level 35 or 40 players would struggle to deal real damage to one.
But Leon’s attack was different.
A deep, black wound opened across the dragon’s neck, darkness seeping into the flesh.
ROOOAR!
The dragon roared in pain and fury, violently swinging its neck and forcing Leon away. Leon slid across the ground, boots carving lines into the stone floor before he stabilized himself.
"YOU INSOLENT BEING," the dragon bellowed. "TODAY... YOU DIE!"
The elemental dragon opened its mouth, elemental energy swirling violently inside. The pressure skyrocketed.
But Leon didn’t move. He didn’t dodge.
Because he knew exactly what would happen next.
His eyes turned silvery-white.
A massive pressure erupted from his body, clashing violently with the dragon’s presence and forcing the air itself to tremble.
Ding!
[Celestial Might has activated.]
"Knew it," Leon said, a confident grin spreading across his face. "I understand how this thing works now."

chapters.title: Chapter 90: Killing The Guardian Dragon of Elements, Blood Heart is Recharged
paragraphs: [Celestial Might has activated.]
The instant the massive pressure erupted from Leon’s body, the entire chamber reacted.
When that overwhelming presence reached the guardian dragon, its enormous body shuddered uncontrollably.
"What—"
The dragon froze.
The pressure pressing down on it was something it had never experienced before.
Not when it stood among other dragons.
Not when it clashed with powerful enemies in the past.
Not even during the countless centuries it had spent guarding this temple.
This feeling was different. It wasn’t fear. Nor intimidation. Those were things the dragon was familiar with.
This was something far beyond that, something it couldn’t properly define or understand.
It felt ancient, absolute, and utterly detached from conventional power.
The sensation alone forced the elemental dragon to shut its mouth, disrupting the spell it had been charging. It wasn’t a conscious decision. Its body simply refused to continue.
"You are..." the guardian dragon muttered, its voice low and strained. "...what the hell are you?"
Leon didn’t answer. Instead, he grinned calmly and shifted his attention to the panel floating before him.
[Guardian Dragon of Elements (Temple Boss)]
[Combat Power: 70,000]
The debuff had worked. Perfectly.
A full thirty percent reduction, applied cleanly even against a being like this.
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly. Its combat power was now lower than his own.
Still, that didn’t mean the fight was suddenly easy.
Combat Power was just a representation of raw strength, stats, and overall capability.
Experience, intelligence, and hidden abilities still mattered greatly.
Leon knew that better than anyone. With the right tricks, a weaker opponent could kill a stronger one.
Likewise, even with higher Combat Power, carelessness could still lead to defeat.
Leon himself was living proof of that. Even when the dragon had been at its full strength of 100,000 Combat Power, his [Shadow Slash] had severely injured it.
If he had managed to land that attack one or two more times, the guardian dragon would already be dead. That fact alone explained its fury.
Yet even now, with its power heavily reduced, the dragon showed no hesitation.
"I have refrained from using this spell," the guardian dragon said slowly, its voice echoing through the chamber, "because it is what I consider to be my strongest one."
The elements around it began to stir violently.
"But someone like you..." it continued, its eyes narrowing, "...deserves nothing."
STORM OF ELEMENTS!
The guardian dragon spread its wings to their full extent, completely overshadowing Leon. The chamber shook as if it were about to collapse.
In an instant, all four elements erupted.
Fire, water, wind, and earth condensed together, forming a massive, chaotic storm that engulfed the entire chamber.
The air twisted violently as elemental energy raged in every direction.
Leon didn’t panic.
Vision Enhancement!
His eyes glowed faintly as the skill activated, allowing him to see the flow of elemental energy clearly.
Fwoosh!
Leon leapt sideways just as a pillar of fire erupted beneath his feet, scorching the stone floor.
A moment later, the ground cracked violently as earth spikes shot upward where he had just been standing.
He continued moving, dodging with precise timing as water blades sliced through the air and violent gusts of wind attempted to slam him into the pillars.
"You can..." the elemental dragon muttered, genuine shock coloring its voice. "You can see the elements?"
Its eyes widened.
"This doesn’t even make sense...!"
Leon didn’t respond. He simply kept dodging. Again and again.
Each movement was clean. Each step perfectly timed.
Watching this, rage surged through the guardian dragon.
It roared furiously and lunged forward, its massive claws slashing through the air toward Leon.
SLASH!
Leon raised his sword and met the attack head-on.
The clash echoed loudly through the chamber as Leon was pushed back a few steps—but he held his ground.
The smile on his face widened slightly.
If the dragon had attacked him like that when its Combat Power was still at 100,000, Leon knew he would not have been able to block it so cleanly.
But now?
"I win," Leon muttered.
He ducked beneath another surge of elemental energy and dashed forward. In one smooth motion, he swung his sword upward, targeting the dragon’s neck once more.
SLASH!
The blade cut deep. Dark energy seeped into the wound as the dragon roared in pain.
ROOOOAR!
"YOU... HUMAN...!"
The guardian dragon thrashed violently, blood spraying across the stone floor. Its rage and pain mixed together, shaking the entire chamber.
Leon didn’t press forward immediately.
Instead, he stepped back and began focusing his power, channeling mana steadily into his sword.
"I have guarded this place..." the guardian dragon bellowed, its voice filled with fury, "...for longer than I can remember!"
Its eyes burned with hatred as it stared at Leon.
"AND SOMEONE LIKE YOU SHALL NOT PASS!"
Leon remained calm.
Then—
Crescent Slash!
A crescent-shaped wave of dark energy launched forward, cutting through the air with terrifying speed.
SLASH!
The attack struck the dragon’s already weakened neck.
This time, it was enough. The guardian dragon’s head separated cleanly from its body.
For a brief moment, everything went silent.
Then the massive body collapsed, crashing heavily against the stone floor. The decapitated head rolled several meters before coming to a stop, its eyes slowly losing their glow.
The guardian dragon was dead.
"...Phew," Leon exhaled as he lowered his sword. "I actually didn’t expect that to work so cleanly."
Ding!
[You have killed "Guardian Dragon of Elements"]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
"Nice."
Leon relaxed slightly and instinctively reached to open his [Storage Space].
After all, the stronger the opponent, the better the drops usually were. And dragons, especially one guarding something this important, were known to drop incredible items.
He was already anticipating what kind of rewards he would find.
But just as he was about to open it—
Ding!
[Your "Blood Heart" has recharged.]
"Oh shit," Leon muttered, his eyes widening. A wide grin spread across his face. "Guess it doesn’t take that long to recharge after all."
Still, the timing made him pause. It was strange.
The [Blood Heart] had recharged after killing this single monster even though Leon had killed many others before.
And the description of the item clearly stated:
[Once used, only upon killing a certain amount of monsters will the usage reset. The monsters cannot be much weaker than the user.]
Leon thought about it for a moment.
It wasn’t just about quantity. It was about strength.
Perhaps the [Blood Heart] recharged faster depending on how strong the opponent was.
And the [Guardian Dragon of Elements] had been far stronger than Leon when they first clashed.
’That’s why it mentions monsters weaker than the user,’ Leon thought, nodding to himself. ’It measures both number and strength.’
That realization satisfied him.
If that was the case, then in the future, when he fought more powerful enemies, the [Blood Heart] would recharge much more frequently.
Leon liked that a lot. Before using it again, though, he finally opened his [Storage Space].
And the contents made him pause.
[Key of Elements (Unique): Opens the gate leading to the secret of the "Elemental Temple".]
[Guardian Dragon of Elements Essence: Consuming will increase Spirit by 100 and Constitution by 50.]

[Elemental Dragon Armor (Mythical): +2,000 Defense, +1,200 Spirit, +1,000 Constitution, +500 Agility. Protects slightly against elemental attacks. Requirement: Have at least two out of the four basic elemental sub-talents.]
[Elemental Dragon Head (Trophy): Proof that you have defeated the "Guardian Dragon of Elements". May be useful in the future.]
"...Damn."
Out of all the items, the one that immediately caught Leon’s attention was the [Key of Elements].
He summoned it into his hand. The key glowed softly, imbued with the power of all four elements.
Just holding it, Leon could feel a faint resonance coming from the massive gate at the end of the chamber.
There was no doubt about it. This key was meant for that gate. And the implications were massive.
It meant that anyone who discovered the [Elemental Temple] was forced to defeat the guardian dragon in order to proceed.
And because finding the temple required possessing all four elemental sub-talents, even Eternal-Level individuals who stood at the very peak had never discovered it.
They never met the conditions. Which meant, everything had aligned perfectly for Leon.
He stepped forward toward the massive gate.
And the moment he did—
Ding!
[Do you wish to use the "Key of Elements" to open the "Elemental Gate"?]
[Yes] [Hell yeah]
Leon stared at the options.
"...Hm," he said thoughtfully. "I wonder which choice I’m picking."

chapters.title: Chapter 91: Blessing Something Once Again, The Dragon Head Trophy
paragraphs: [Do you wish to use the "Key of Elements" to open the "Elemental Gate"?]
[Yes] [Hell yeah]
"...I guess that’s to be expected."
Leon wasn’t even surprised.
Much like the moment when he had been asked whether or not he wanted to proceed to the second assessment immediately, the system simply did not allow him to choose "no."
His [Celestial] title was the reason.
Once something appeared in front of him as a true path forward, he was forced to walk it.
The fact that it activated even in a situation like this was... interesting.
It meant that in the future, there would likely be many more moments where Leon would have no option but to move forward, no matter how dangerous or uncertain the outcome was.
It didn’t bother him. If anything, it was good to know early.
Still, Leon didn’t rush into it right away. He casually cast the panel aside.
Unlike before, there was no time limit forcing him to make an immediate decision. The gate wasn’t going anywhere.
So instead of stepping through right away, he decided to take care of everything else first.
Preparation always came first. The very first thing Leon did was consume the [Guardian Dragon of Elements Essence].
The moment he did, a warm sensation spread through his body.
[Spirit +100, Constitution +50]
Leon exhaled slowly as his body adjusted.
"That’s a pretty nice boost."
Next, he equipped the [Elemental Dragon Armor (Mythical)].
The moment the armor settled onto his body, he could feel the difference immediately. It was heavier than his previous one, but in a good way: stable, solid, and protective.
Leon flexed his arm once, feeling the flow of mana through it.
"Well," he said, scratching his chin, "this armor is good enough that I might actually keep it for a long time."
Then his gaze sharpened slightly.
"And now that I know the [Blood Heart] doesn’t take that long to recharge..."
A grin formed on his face.
"...might as well do it."
Leon focused inward, reaching for the unique special item bound directly to him.
His heartbeat slowed, then synced, aligning perfectly with the pulsing rhythm of the [Blood Heart].
The sensation was familiar now.
And then—
Ding!
[You have used the "Blood Heart" on the "Elemental Dragon Armor"]
[You have blessed the "Elemental Dragon Armor"]
Fwoosh!
A surge of crimson light burst outward, wrapping itself around Leon’s body. The glow seeped into the armor, causing it to shine repeatedly before slowly settling down.
When the light faded, thin crimson lines had formed along the surface of the armor, tracing patterns between the elemental engravings.
Leon immediately opened the item’s panel.
[Elemental Dragon Armor (Mythical): +2,000 Defense, +1,200 Spirit, +1,000 Constitution, +500 Agility. Protects slightly from elemental attacks.]
[Blood Heart Blessing: Able to cast "Storm of Elements".]
As expected, the armor’s stats hadn’t changed. The [Blood Heart] didn’t seem to directly increase numerical values.
But the blessing itself? That was far more interesting.
Unlike the blessing on his [Void Staff], this one granted him an entirely new active ability. A real one.
Leon quickly checked the details.
[Storm of Elements (Blessing): Summon the power of your four basic elements into a storm in a nearby area, able to disrupt opponents.]
"...Damn."
It clearly wasn’t on the same level as the dragon’s version of the spell, but that didn’t matter.
It was still a powerful new skill, and one that synergized perfectly with Leon’s talents.
Ding!
[The "Blood Heart" has gone on cooldown. Please recharge it by killing monsters!]
"Right."
Leon nodded calmly. All things considered, he was extremely satisfied.
Between the stat boosts, the new armor, and the blessing, he had grown noticeably stronger in a very short time.
He could have also used the [Blood Heart] on his [Undead Sword +3], but he hesitated.
’I’ll probably replace that sword soon anyway,’ Leon thought.
Still...
’Although,’ he admitted to himself, ’based on what I saw with the previous blessings... the one on that sword might actually strengthen my undead.’
Leon hadn’t forgotten about his [Basic Necromancy (E-Level)] sub-talent.
The problem was simple: his undead were still too weak to be useful.
Using them right now was more of a liability than an advantage.
Even so, Leon didn’t plan to abandon the talent. In the future, he wanted to make proper use of it.
The best way to do that was to upgrade it, but that was easier said than done.
Opponents with necromancy-related talents were rare. And the stronger a talent was, the rarer it became. Some only appeared on a handful of monsters in the entire domains.
Still, Leon wasn’t the type to give up. He’d find a way eventually.
Finally, his gaze shifted to the last item dropped by the dragon: [Elemental Dragon Head (Trophy)]
This item was the second most interesting one in the batch. And not because of its stats.
But because Leon already knew a possible use for it.
In the [Higher Domain], players would eventually encounter an NPC known as the [Hunter]. An incredibly powerful existence.
One who could grant massive rewards, unlock special shops, and even provide access to some of the most dangerous and lucrative quests in the entire domain.
But earning his favor wasn’t easy. The [Hunter] didn’t care about words or promises. He cared about proof.
About things he deemed "worthy." And what could possibly be more worthy than a literal dragon’s head?
Leon couldn’t help but grin.
’If this works... things could get very interesting.’
He stored the trophy inside his [Storage Space], making a mental note to remember it when the time was right.
Once everything was done, Leon finally turned back to the floating panel.
Without hesitation, he pressed the second option: [Hell yeah]
Fwoosh! Ding!
[Opening the "Elemental Gate"]
Immediately, the [Key of Elements] floated out of Leon’s storage space on its own and drifted toward the massive gate.
Click!
The key slid perfectly into the lock. With a heavy rumble, the gate unlocked and split open from both sides.
A powerful aura poured out from beyond it, washing over Leon in waves.
For some reason, Leon felt a bad feeling creep up his spine. But that didn’t stop him. He stepped forward.
Fwoosh!
Leon passed through the elemental gate.
SLAM!
The moment he emerged on the other side, the gate shut violently behind him. There was no going back.
Ding!
[Grab the reward of your assessment, Celestial.]
"Oh?" Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly. "So these are my rewards."
After everything he had gone through, he fully expected something special.
Leon looked around. He was now standing in a massive room, though smaller than the previous chamber.
On the left side stood a tall altar. It was ancient, cracked, and worn, yet it glowed faintly with power.
Streams of elemental energy flowed through the cracks like glowing veins.
Leon could feel it immediately. This altar wasn’t decorative. It was something he could interact with.
On the right side of the room stood a small pedestal. An item rested on top of it, glowing faintly.
And finally, in the center of the room, floating in midair, surrounded by several strands of elemental light... Was an egg.
A crimson egg. It radiated an overwhelming aura, one so powerful that Leon didn’t need a panel to understand a single thing.
Whatever was inside it was terrifying. This was the reward room of the [Elemental Temple].
A place no one had ever reached before. No player before him had set foot here.
That alone spoke volumes about what Leon had just accomplished.
Leon’s gaze shifted back to the pedestal.
The item resting there looked like some kind of syringe, filled with an unfamiliar liquid that shimmered softly.
"...Alright," Leon said with a grin. "Time to get my rewards."
With that, he stepped forward toward the three rewards awaiting him.

chapters.title: Chapter 92: Enhancement Frenzy Liquid, SS-Level Master of Elements Sub-Talent
paragraphs: The first reward Leon walked toward was the syringe filled with golden liquid.
It floated slightly above its pedestal, the liquid inside shimmering faintly as if it were alive.
Even without a panel, Leon could feel that it wasn’t ordinary. His instincts screamed value. He didn’t hesitate.
Leon stepped forward and grabbed the syringe, his fingers wrapping around the cold glass before lifting it closer to his eyes. Only then did the system panel appear.
Ding!
[Enhancement Frenzy Liquid (Ancient): Injecting will guarantee the next enhancement to work (3/3 uses left)]1
"DAMN!"
Leon’s eyes widened instantly. He hadn’t expected anything remotely like this. No, he hadn’t even imagined it.
In all his fifteen years inside [Eternal Ascension], he had never once heard of an item that could guarantee an enhancement.1
Enhancements were one of the most brutal systems in the game.
Even with expensive materials, rare catalysts, and specialized professions, success was never assured.
Failures destroyed items permanently.
That was why enhancement stones and luck-boosting charms sold for a high price.
But this? This erased the risk entirely.
Guaranteeing an enhancement was something players in the [Higher Domain] or [Eternal Domain] would quite literally kill for.
Guild wars had started over far less.
This syringe alone could sell for millions of [Eternal Coins], depending on who bought it and what they intended to enhance.
Legendary weapons. Ancient armor. Sub-talents at the edge of evolution.
Leon’s heartbeat quickened slightly as he realized just how dangerous it was to even possess this thing.
Without wasting another second, he stored the syringe inside his [Storage Space].
’No one should know,’ He swore it silently.
He wouldn’t mention it. Not even to himself out loud. An item like this was an invitation to disaster if the wrong person found out.
He also knew better than to use it now. Using it at his current stage would be stupid.
Three uses. That was all it had. Each one needed to be saved for something truly irreplaceable.
Leon took a deep breath and forced himself to calm down.
’Later’, he thought. ’Way later.’
Once his excitement settled, he turned his gaze toward the left side of the room. The altar stood there.
It was carved from pale stone, covered in ancient markings that pulsed faintly with elemental energy.
Unlike the syringe, it didn’t float or shine extravagantly. It simply existed, heavy and immovable, like it had been waiting for someone for a very long time.
Leon approached it cautiously. As soon as he extended his hand toward the altar, a system sound rang out.
Ding!
[You have defeated the "Guardian Dragon of Elements" and shown your true mastery of the basic elements.]
[As a result... you shall become a master of them.]
Fwoosh!
A new panel appeared immediately after.
[Do you wish to sacrifice all your four main elemental talents to the altar?]
[Yes] [Why not?]
"Hm."
Leon frowned slightly. This was far more confusing than the syringe.
The wording was strange. Sacrifice his four main elemental sub-talents? That wasn’t a small thing.
Those sub-talents could help his spell become much stronger after all. Some of them were already at high ranks.
Losing them outright would normally be unthinkable.
And yet... this was the reward for completing the assessment.
An assessment guarded by a dragon. A dragon that had tested his control over every element he possessed.
Leon narrowed his eyes and thought carefully.
’If this altar just deletes them, that would be ridiculous’, he thought. ’But that makes no sense.’
"This is the assessment’s reward," Leon muttered, opening his eyes again. "So it must be good."
The system never gave meaningless rewards, especially not after something like that fight.
After a full minute of silence, Leon made his choice.
He selected [Why not?].
Ding!
[You have sacrificed "Absolute Flame Control (A-Level)" to the "Elemental Altar"]
[You have sacrificed "Wind Dominion (A-Level)" to the "Elemental Altar"]
[You have sacrificed "Deep Water Affinity (B-Level)"...]
[You have sacrificed "Earth Affinity (C-Level)"...]
Fwish!
Four orbs burst out of Leon’s body in that instant.
Each one glowed with a different color: red, green, gray, and brown, representing the four elemental sub-talents he had just given up.
The orbs floated briefly in the air before slamming into the altar one after another. With each impact, the altar trembled.
The ancient markings carved into its surface lit up, growing brighter and brighter as elemental energy flooded into it.
And then—
Ding!
[You shall be blessed.]
BOOM!
A blinding ray of light erupted from the altar and struck Leon directly in the chest. His entire body jolted violently.
Pure elemental aura surged through him, leaking from his mouth, his eyes, even his skin.
His vision blurred as power rushed into his core, overwhelming his senses for several long seconds.
When the light finally faded, Leon stood there breathing heavily, his hair fluttering slightly as residual energy dispersed.
A new panel appeared.
Ding!
[You have received the SS-Level Sub-Talent: "Master of Elements"]
"DAMN!"
Leon didn’t even try to hide his reaction. This was absurd.
This sub-talent was somehow even stronger than the guardian dragon’s own [Elemental Master] talent. That alone was proof of how ridiculous it was.
Anyone who obtained this would immediately change their entire build.
Warriors would turn into spellblades. Assassins into elemental burst monsters.
And mages? Mages would ascend. Leon quickly opened the sub-talent’s description.

[Master of Elements (SS-Level): You can master any and all basic elements (not advanced or supreme) perfectly as long as you have a basic understanding of them, allowing your spells and attacks to become much stronger.]
[Current Elements: Fire, Water, Earth, Wind.]
Leon stared at the panel, then slowly grinned.
It didn’t look flashy. But he understood it perfectly.
Every single one of his sacrificed sub-talents—regardless of their original rank—had effectively been condensed into a single SS-Level talent.
Even his former C-Level Earth Affinity was now operating at an SS-Level standard.
That meant sharper control. Stronger spells. Better efficiency. Less waste.
Everything elemental he used from now on would be on an entirely different level.
’I wonder how destructive [Powerful Fireball] and [Storm of Lightning] are now’, Leon thought.
Then his eyes shifted to one specific line: [Current Elements.]
The fact that it existed meant only one thing.
"This can be expanded," Leon muttered.
He focused on the sub-talent, testing his theory.
Ding!
[Do you wish to sacrifice "Supreme Lightning Affinity (A-Level)" to the "Master of Elements" sub-talent?]
"Yes!"
Ding!
["Lightning" has been added to your elements list.]
Leon opened the panel again.
[Current Elements: Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Lightning.]
"Bingo."
This confirmed it.
Even if Leon acquired an F-Level sub-talent related to a basic element, he could sacrifice it and instantly elevate it to SS-Level through this ability.
Of course, it wasn’t limitless.
Beep!
[You cannot sacrifice "Darkness" and "Blood" as they are advanced elements.]
Leon wasn’t surprised. Elements were classified into three categories: Basic, Advanced and Supreme.
Fire, Wind, Water, Lightning, and Earth were basic.
Darkness and Blood were advanced.
As for supreme elements... they were on an entirely different level.
They were so rare that Leon only knew of one: Void.
In his previous life, the player who possessed Void came from an eternal-level world. Someone so powerful they could fight entire armies alone.
If Leon ever acquired a supreme element... He would truly rise.
Unlike basic and advanced elements, supreme elements unlocked unique abilities and could actively reshape battles.
Still, Leon was more than satisfied. He turned toward the final reward. If it could even be called that.
Unlike the syringe and the altar, this one was simply... an egg.
A crimson egg resting quietly on the stone floor.
Leon immediately grew cautious. Eggs meant beasts.
"That’s probably what the dragon was protecting," Leon muttered as he stepped closer. "Gotta be careful."
If dragons wanted it safe, then it wasn’t ordinary. As he approached, a final panel appeared.
Ding!
[Primordial Dragon of Chaos (Unhatched)]
[Rank: Divine]
[Hatching Time: 4,228 years, 327 days.]
Should I, at some point, reveal Leon’s entire status panel, including all the items he is wearing right now?
It would only be done once in a while but would help contextualise what he has.

It would only be done once in a while but would help contextualise what he has.

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Primordial Dragon of Chaos, 4,000 Years?!
paragraphs: [Primordial Dragon of Chaos (Unhatched)]
[Rank: Divine]
[Hatching Time: 4,228 years, 327 days.]
Leon stared at the panel for a long moment, his expression complicated.
Of course, he understood immediately what this meant.
This egg belonged to a beast, one that could be tamed.

In [Eternal Ascension], beasts weren’t rare, but powerful ones were. Players could tame beasts to assist them in battle, to travel faster across dangerous regions, or purely for utility if the beast possessed strong passive abilities.
Some players even built their entire playstyle around beasts.
Leon had seen it himself in his previous life. Players who barely fought directly, instead commanding terrifying creatures that crushed enemies for them.
Some had entire stables filled with beasts, constantly replacing weaker ones with stronger acquisitions.
And then there were the truly absurd cases.
Leon had once seen a beast, controlled by a top-ranked player, wipe out an entire city by itself. Walls, defenses, NPCs, monsters... all gone in minutes.
Still, Leon’s gaze drifted back to one specific word on the panel.
"Divine," he thought.
That alone changed everything.
Divine-ranked beasts were on an entirely different level. They weren’t just strong, they were existences bordering on godhood.
If one grew fully and awakened all of its potential, it would stand on the same level as gods themselves.
And this wasn’t just any beast. It was a dragon.
Dragons were already rare to the point of absurdity. Leon could count on one hand the number of players he had known who possessed dragon beasts in his past life.
And even among dragons, this one stood out: [Primordial Dragon of Chaos]. Just the name alone radiated danger.
"Primordial" meant ancient beyond measure. An existence that had existed before most things.
"Chaos" meant unpredictability, destruction, and raw power.
Leon didn’t need a detailed description to understand how terrifying this beast could become.
The dragons guarding the temple suddenly made sense.
They hadn’t just been protecting the place. They had been protecting this. Waiting for it to hatch.
Still... Leon’s eyes dropped to the final line.
[Hatching Time: 4,228 years, 327 days.]
"...That’s insane."
That was impossibly long.
By the time this thing hatched naturally, Leon would either be long dead, or a legitimate god.
For a brief moment, the thought crossed his mind.
Is this even worth it? But the thought vanished almost instantly.
There was no way the [Heavenly One] would place something like this here without expecting someone to eventually obtain it.
Leon clenched his fist slightly.
"There has to be a way."
There were countless hidden systems in [Eternal Ascension]. Accelerated growth methods. Time compression zones. Rituals. Sacrifices. Forbidden items.
This egg wasn’t meant to be decorative.
It was meant to hatch. At least... Leon hoped so.
After a moment of hesitation, he stepped closer and placed his hand on the egg.
The moment he touched it, the elemental aura keeping it afloat dissolved and flowed inward.
Ding!
[You have obtained the egg of the "Primordial Dragon of Chaos"]
[Details: An existence that all dragons worship and fear, though it will take time for it to hatch.]
The egg shimmered once, and then vanished.
It seeped directly into Leon’s body, disappearing completely.
Leon didn’t panic. He could feel it.
Much like the [Blood Heart], the egg was now directly tied to his soul. He could access its panel at any time, but no one else could see it.
That meant only one thing. Even if he died, it wouldn’t drop.
And more importantly... No one could steal it.
’Good,’ Leon thought.
If anyone discovered the existence of this beast, it would be a catastrophe.
Entire guilds would mobilize. Kingdoms might get involved. Higher Domain players could intervene the moment he stepped there.
This wasn’t something he could protect yet. His thoughts shifted briefly.
’I wonder if Emilia’s talent would help with this thing.’
One of Emilia’s talent passives guaranteed absolute loyalty from her beasts, no matter what.
But the wording mattered. "Her" beasts. Leon planned for this dragon to be his.
Whether Emilia could influence it, or whether she should, was something he would worry about later.
First, he needed to figure out how to hatch it.
Fwoosh!
Before he could think further, the system interrupted him.
Ding!
[A global announcement is about to be broadcasted through all 1,000 Lower Domains.]
"Huh?"
Leon froze. Global announcements weren’t rare, but this phrasing made his heart beat faster.
All 1,000 Lower Domains? That wasn’t normal.
Then he read the panel that followed. His eyes widened.
"OH SHIT."
Ding!
[Player "Celestial" is the first in the history of "Eternal Ascension" to conquer the "Elemental Temple"]
The announcement rang out. Ten times in a row.
It wasn’t subtle.
Whether players were inside dungeons, walking through cities, hiding in forests, or even sleeping, they saw it.
The system made sure of it.
Normally, global announcements were restricted to your own [Lower Domain]. Something happening in Domain #17 wouldn’t concern Domain #432.
But this? This crossed all boundaries.
The last time Leon remembered something like this happening was when the first stronghold had been established in the Lower Domains, and the guild behind it survived the beast tide.
Leon exhaled slowly.
"Haha..."
He rubbed his forehead.
"I wanted my name to spread," he said with a grin, "but this is a bit much."
This meant everyone saw it. Even players nearing their ascension to the [High Domain]
Celestial. That name was now burned into the minds of millions.
Ding!
[You have managed to complete the S-Rank Assessment and conquer the "Elemental Temple", a feat no one had ever achieved before. You have been rewarded with 50 Reputation Points.]
[Your reputation has reached 200. You will now gain 25 additional attributes per level.]
Leon’s grin widened.
"That makes it 150 per level," he thought. "Good enough."
That bonus alone would snowball insanely fast. Before he could linger on it, the air in front of him twisted.
Fwoosh!
A portal appeared in the center of the room. His exit.
Leon didn’t hesitate. He sprinted forward and jumped straight into it.
Ding!
[Transporting to the "Intermediate Divine Temple"]
Light engulfed him. His vision blurred. And a few seconds later—
He stood just outside the S-Rank assessment gate.
"...Welcome back."
Leon turned his head. Emilia was sitting against the gate, her back resting casually against the stone, arms crossed.
The moment she saw him, her grin widened.
"I knew you’d do something crazy." She stood up and stretched.
Meanwhile...
Shadow Assassin Guild, Lower Domain #83.
"I want you all to find me information on this [Celestial]," the guild leader said coldly.
He was a bear beastman, towering over everyone else in the room. His level hovered at 50, and the aura around him was heavy with killing intent.
"He may be in a different [Lower Domain]," the man continued, "but contact all members. No exceptions."
"Yes, boss!"
This was a guild exclusively for assassins.
For the right price, they could eliminate almost any player. The guild leader folded his arms.
’If such an announcement appeared,’ he thought, ’then the reward must be incredible.’
He hadn’t attempted his third assessment in almost a year.
He wanted certainty. But if he could obtain what Celestial had gained... Or kill him and take it...
Then perhaps the path forward would become much easier. His eyes narrowed.
"Find him."

chapters.title: Chapter 94: The Global Announcement’s Effect, Emilia’s Magic Saint Title
paragraphs: Church of Light, Lower Domain #22
"I have a bad feeling about this."
The Archbishop of Light spoke slowly, his fingers clasped together as he stared at the faint glow of the holy sigil before him.
He was a player like any other, but unlike most, he had devoted his entire existence to the [God of Light].
Years ago, he had received what he believed to be a divine calling. A whisper that echoed through his soul, guiding him toward faith, obedience, and worship.
Since then, everything he did revolved around one goal: to be chosen.
To one day stand before his god and have his devotion rewarded.
No one knew yet, but in the near future he would be the [God of Light]’s strongest soldier, meaning he was a target Leon wanted to get rid off.
"Priests," the archbishop said, turning toward the figures kneeling behind him, "the [God of Light] has instructed us to prepare."
The room went silent. No one dared breathe loudly.
"His arrival is soon," the archbishop continued, his tone heavy, "but there is something... unsettling."
He raised his head, eyes narrowing.
"This player," he said, "this one who calls himself [Celestial]. I believe he may affect our glorious church in the future."
Murmurs erupted instantly.
"R-Right! How dare a mere player refer to himself as a divinity!"
"A Celestial? Don’t make me laugh!"
"We must find him! To claim such a name is blasphemy!"
To them, the word Celestial carried meaning. It implied divinity.
And divinity belonged to gods alone. The gods were absolute. Untouchable. Perfect.
Any player who dared place themselves on the same level, whether intentionally or not, was a threat.
And threats were dealt with swiftly. The archbishop closed his eyes.
"Calm yourselves," he said. "We will not act rashly."
He opened them again, light flickering faintly within.
"But remember this," he added. "If this [Celestial] truly walks a path that opposes the will of the gods... then the Church of Light will be the first to judge him."
Lower Domain #667
A dark alleyway stretched between two crumbling stone buildings.
Dim lantern light barely reached the ground.
A woman stood there, her crimson eyes lifted toward the floating system panels that slowly faded from view.
"This..." she muttered.
Her hair shimmered faintly like embers, and a subtle heat radiated from her body even while standing still.
Then, slowly, a small smile appeared on her lips.
"...Interesting."
She had seen Leon’s panel, and thus knew well that his ID was Celestial, so the fact he had appeared before her was a strange coincidence.
She remembered his presence when he spoke to her along with that elf girl.
Still, she trusted no one. Too many had tried to take advantage of her race.
The phoenix race was rare. And rarity attracted hunters.
She had learned that the hard way.
She always rejected being in a party and fought alone as a result, growing stronger thanks to her own talent and capabilities.
But she knew well that in this world, being alone would eventually mean death, as the stength of her foes would increase.
"I’m one of the last in my tribe..." she muttered, "All the others are gone, I can’t let their deaths be in vein."
Phoenixes revived a week after death. Most believed that made them unkillable. They were wrong.
There was a way to kill them permanently. And those who knew it were ruthless.
The reason for that was simple: when a phoenix died, they dropped something precious. A material so rare that entire organizations hunted her people for it.
This material could help a lot, as it could boost immortaility.
Gather enough of it, and one could mimic the phoenix’s regenerative properties.
Still, Celeste vowed to get revenge and hide until she was strong enough to take them on.
’I don’t trust anyone,’ she thought. Her eyes narrowed slightly, ’But that [Celestial] guy...’
She shook her head.
"No."
She wouldn’t get close to anyone. Not yet.
They weren’t even in the same [Lower Domain] anyway.
For now, she would continue alone. Until she was strong enough.
Across the Lower Domains, countless players stared at the same name: Celestial.
All of them had their plans, whether to see what Leon could do, or gain advantage from it.
But none of them truly understood who they were dealing with.
Back at the [Intermediate Divine Temple]
Ding!
[Congratulations to "Celestial" for successfully completing the S-Rank Assessment.]
Leon exhaled slowly.
This was the third announcement echoing through the divine temple.
Celeste’s announcement had rung earlier. Then Emilia’s. Now his.
The place was quiet again.
"I cleared it extremely easily," Emilia said with a grin, stretching her arms. "Honestly, nothing could even hurt me. Before I realized it, I was already at the end."
"As expected," Leon replied, nodding.
S-Rank assessments were rare. Clearing one was even rarer.
Today, only three players had succeeded.
Leon, Emilia. And the phoenix girl.
And among them, Leon was the only one who had gone further, who had gathered all elemental sub-talents and unlocked the [Elemental Temple].
Which meant one thing: rewards.
"You’re gonna be shocked," Emilia said, scratching her chin. "But the only things I gained were the fact I gain 100 attributes per level... and a [Title]."
Leon blinked.
"That’s kind of weak for an S-Rank assessment," he replied honestly. "Unless the title is insane.
Emilia smiled and sent the panel.
Leon read it. Then froze.
"...Holy shit."
[Magic Saint: Multiplies your current Spirit attribute by 5 constantly, making all spells far stronger.]
Leon slowly looked up at her.
"Are you favored by the [Heavenly One] or something?" he asked, genuinely confused. "First a constitution multiplier, now spirit?"
This wasn’t normal at all. Multipliers stacked. And stacked hard.
Based on the trend, her third assessment might give another multiplier entirely: Agility or even Strength.
Who knew? Emilia was already absurdly strong.
At this point, almost no one in the [Lower Domain] could challenge her.
Even the [Guardian Dragon of Elements] Leon fought wouldn’t stand a chance.
One [Divine Beam] with that spirit value would erase it instantly.
Of course, she had already passed her second assessment, so going back wasn’t possible.
Leon had heard of players gaining massive boosts after assessments.
But Emilia was different as it was much stronger. This wasn’t coincidence.
"Can I see your [Combat Power]?" Leon asked. "Just for a second."
Emilia’s grin widened as she sent the panel.
[Combat Power: 132,215]
"...Damn."
The multiplier alone had added tens of thousands of combat power.
"Well," Leon said, patting her head lightly, "I guess that’s good. You don’t even need me anymore."
With this strength, Emilia could walk the [Lower Domain] freely.
At level 25, she could fight level 50 players head-on. And as she leveled up, the gap would only widen.
Yet—
"No," Emilia said calmly, shaking her head. "I’d rather stay with you... forever."
She hesitated at the last word. Leon chuckled.
"It’s been less than a day since we met," he replied. "Let’s wait before using big words."
"Alright," she nodded. But in her mind, she had already chosen.
"I wonder what you got~" she added playfully.
"An SS-Level Sub-Talent," Leon replied. "I’ll show you later."
He didn’t talk about the [Enhancement Frenzy Liquid] nor the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos] egg since it would be stupid.
"Leave."
"Leave!"
Light wrapped around them. And just like that, they vanished from the [Intermediate Divine Temple].

The light faded, and solid ground returned beneath their feet.
Ding!
[You have arrived at "Lower Domain #1"]
Leon took a slow look around as the familiar scenery came into view.
"Hm."
Only now, after completing their second assessment, was the number of their [Lower Domain] finally revealed.

Leon did not answer immediately. His eyes narrowed slightly as several thoughts connected in his mind.
’[Novice Village #1] and now [Lower Domain #1],’ he thought. ’Just like last time.’
In his previous life, he had also started in these exact locations. Back then, he never questioned it. He had assumed it was random, just another roll of the dice by the system.
But now, after everything he had seen, Leon was no longer convinced randomness played such a big role.
"This might not be a coincidence," he muttered quietly.
"What was that?" Emilia asked.
"Nothing important," Leon replied. "I was just thinking out loud."
He glanced upward briefly, as if expecting another panel to appear.
"I still don’t remember my [Higher Domain] number," he added after a moment.
It was something he truly could not recall from his past life. Either he had never paid attention to it, or it simply had not mattered back then.
In the end, it did not change his plans. He already knew what he needed to do.
Leon turned around, and the thick gray haze of the [Land of Mist] stretched behind them.
The moment they had been teleported back, they had appeared beyond it, safely on the other side.
If someone wanted to return to [Moon City], they would need to pass through that zone again.
Emilia followed his gaze and smiled faintly.
"That place felt creepy the first time," she said. "But now it doesn’t really feel dangerous anymore."
Leon nodded slowly.
"I don’t think any monster in there can actually challenge you at this point," he replied. "Except maybe one."
Emilia tilted her head slightly.
"Hmm... well, even if there is one, it shouldn’t be a problem," she said with a shrug. "At least now I can actually help instead of just standing behind you."
"You were already useful before," Leon said calmly. "Your buffs alone made a big difference. But now it’s true, you can fight on your own."
That alone changed many things.
Leon’s goal was still the same as always. He wanted to grow so strong that not even the gods would be able to threaten him. That path was one he would walk no matter what.
Still, having powerful people beside him made that journey safer.
Someone like Emilia watching his back meant fewer blind spots and fewer mistakes.
Leon trusted her strength. And more importantly, he trusted her intentions.
As they turned forward and began walking, the scenery ahead slowly shifted.
A massive city rose in the distance. Even from far away, it was impossible to miss.
Tall walls stretched across the horizon, layered with towers and banners. Roads converged toward it from every direction, packed with players heading in and out.
"Behold," Leon said as the city grew clearer with every step. "This is where things really start."
Emilia raised an eyebrow, "This place looks huge."
"It is," Leon replied. "Unlike the first half of the [Lower Domain], this city is the main point of interest from now on."
As they approached, its sheer scale became obvious.
It was far larger than both [Hub City] and [Moon City] combined.
This was the center of the second half of the [Lower Domain], where players from level twenty five to fifty would gather.
Most would spend the majority of their time here, whether to trade, rest, or prepare for dangerous explorations.
Everything beyond this point revolved around this city.
The surrounding regions were filled with stronger monsters, rare resources, and opportunities that simply did not exist earlier.
"Let me guess," Emilia said as they broke into a light run toward the gates. "There’s another hidden quest here."
Leon shook his head, "Surprisingly, no."
"Oh?" Emilia looked at him with interest.
"There’s something better though" Leon replied. "Something much more useful."
Before she could ask further, a large system panel appeared before them as they got close enough.
Ding!
[Myriad Race City]
Emilia slowed her pace and looked around.
Players of countless races filled the area. Humans, beastmen, elves, dwarves, orcs, and races she had never even seen before all moved through the massive gates.
Now the name made sense.
"This really is a city for everyone," Emilia said quietly.
Leon nodded.
"If you remember anything about this place," he said, "remember that."
They reached the gates, where heavily armored guards stood watch.
Every one of them was level fifty. Leon tried to inspect one out of habit.
Beep!
[You are not allowed to see that.]
His eyes narrowed slightly.
"So they’re blocking appraisal entirely," he thought.
That usually meant one of two things. Either the guards were protected by special enchantments, or the city simply did not want players peeking too much.
"Don’t do that again, filthy human."
A deep voice rumbled beside him. Leon turned his head to see a towering orc guard glaring down at him.
"Or you might regret it."
The hostility was clear. Between that reaction and what Leon remembered about this city, it was easy to see the pattern.
This place was controlled by orcs. And not the friendly kind.
The city lord himself was an orc native, someone Leon remembered all too well from his past life.
He was strong. Cruel. And far from fair.
Leon did not respond to the threat. He simply looked away calmly as another panel appeared.
Ding!
[To enter "Myriad Race City", you must pay 1,000 Eternal Coins as a one-time fee.]
Emilia sighed.
"That feels like a scam," she muttered. "I think I have enough, though."
"It’s a one time fee," Leon replied. "We only pay it once. I’ve got more than enough anyway."
That was true. If Leon ever needed more money, he had plenty of options.
He could sell items, equipment, or even some of the sub-talent scrolls he obtained in the [Elemental Lands].
Money was not an immediate concern. Without hesitation, Leon confirmed the payment.
Ding!
[You have sent 2,000 Eternal Coins to Myriad Orc Guard.]
He paid for both of them, making things simpler.
The guards stepped aside, and Leon and Emilia walked through the massive gates.
Disgusted stares followed them. Orcs did not hide their expressions, and it was obvious they did not like humans entering their city.
Neither Leon nor Emilia cared. As long as the rules were followed, the guards would not attack.
And rules were something Leon had no intention of breaking here.
As they entered the city proper, Leon opened his [Friends List].
As expected, several messages were waiting for him.
[DivineWind (David): Holy hell brother, how do you even keep doing this?!]
[DestinyArcher (Eleonore): I told the others not to say your ID or that we’re friends with you, don’t worry •ᴗ•.]
[ShadowAaron: Haha, I knew something crazy was about to happen. Show me more!]
[AliceSupports: W-Wow, you’re even more of a bigshot than I thought!]
Leon chuckled quietly as he read them. It was nice to see their reactions.
Still, Eleonore’s message stood out the most.
He quickly replied, thanking her. She had done the right thing.
If anyone discovered that they were connected to the player known as Celestial, it would put a massive target on their backs.
And that was the last thing Leon wanted.
As for Alice’s message, Leon shook his head slightly.
"Why does she even stutter in text," he muttered with a small smile. "It’s not like I can hear her."
Emilia glanced at him, "Talking to yourself again?"
"The others sent messages," Leon replied.
"Oh! I also received a message from Eleonore," Emilia grinned, "I guess she was worried about me as well."
They continued forward, fully entering the city streets.
Massive buildings stretched upward, shops lined every major road, and players moved in organized chaos all around them.
Just like that, Leon and Emilia had officially stepped into the second half of the [Lower Domain]. Into [Myriad Race City].
And this time, things were only going to get more dangerous.

chapters.title: Chapter 96: The Crimson Egg’s Shockwave, To The Myriad Arena
paragraphs: It was currently night in [Myriad Race City], and just like Leon expected, nightfall did not mean silence. It meant entertainment.
Lights of every color filled the streets, magical lanterns floating in the air and crystal lamps embedded into buildings.
Music echoed from taverns and open halls, mixed with laughter, shouting, and the constant hum of movement.
Players from every possible race wandered through the streets without restraint, and their levels varied wildly.
Leon noticed level 30 players eagerly talking to level 50 veterans, asking for advice or guidance.
Others had small stalls set up on the side of the road, selling weapons, armor, potions, and strange materials harvested from dangerous zones.
Some were bargaining loudly, while others simply observed, eyes sharp and cautious.
Many players chose to remain in the [Lower Domain] for a long time, and this city was the reason.
As long as someone was strong enough, boredom simply did not exist here.
There was always something happening. There was always someone stronger to learn from or someone weaker to dominate.
Of course, danger existed beyond the city walls.
The lands surrounding [Myriad Race City] were filled with deadly monsters and unpredictable zones.
But those dangers were optional. The city itself was a sanctuary of sorts, chaotic but controlled.
Leon decided it would be best to take a short break.
Not because he felt tired, and not because Emilia looked exhausted, but because caution mattered.
Fatigue could appear at the worst possible moment, especially in battle. Resting ahead of time was always the smarter option.
There was also something else on his mind.
He wanted to show Emilia the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos] egg.
He wanted to see if her talent could perceive anything unusual about it. Even if nothing happened, it was still worth trying.
As they walked toward the row of inns scattered across the city, the atmosphere around them shifted slightly.
The streets grew livelier, and the type of entertainment became more obvious.
"Hey there, handsome~"
A rabbit-eared girl stepped directly into Leon’s path, her long ears twitching slightly as she smiled brightly.
Her outfit was revealing, clearly designed to draw attention.
"If you want, we have several services available tonight, and I promise you will not regret it."
"Not interested," Leon replied without slowing down. "Find someone else."
He continued walking, Emilia right beside him.
"Tch. Rude," the rabbit-eared girl muttered as she crossed her arms.
Leon did not even glance back.
After a few seconds, Emilia tilted her head slightly, realization dawning on her face.
"Wait," she said, "was that one of those places?"
"Yes," Leon replied with a small grin. "And I do not need that kind of thing. It is a waste of time. I want to show you something instead."
Emilia smiled warmly and leaned slightly closer to him.
"Plus, you have me," she said playfully.
Leon paused for half a second, "...Sure."
They continued walking through the city, taking in the sights.
After around ten minutes, Leon and Emilia finally found a quiet inn that looked sturdy and well maintained.
The sign outside glowed softly, and unlike the louder taverns, this place seemed focused on rest rather than celebration.
They stepped inside and rented a room without trouble.
Once inside, Leon made sure to lock the door carefully.
He closed the windows and activated the basic privacy barrier provided by the inn.
Only when he was certain no one could see or sense them did he relax.
"Take a look," Leon said calmly.
He reached into his system inventory and pulled out the crimson egg of the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos].
The egg glowed faintly, its surface etched with strange patterns that looked almost alive.
The moment it appeared in the room though, everything changed.
BOOM!
A terrifying pulse of aura erupted from the egg, exploding outward like a shockwave.
The air trembled violently, and the walls shook as if struck by an invisible force. The pressure was overwhelming, filled with chaos and dominance.
Leon’s eyes widened in shock.
"Oh shit!"
He reacted instantly, shoving the egg back into his system inventory.
The aura vanished just as suddenly as it appeared, leaving behind a heavy silence.
"I hope you saw that," Leon muttered.
Emilia stood frozen in place, her eyes wide.
"What the hell was that thing?" she whispered. "That was a beast egg..."
"Did you see the status window?" Leon asked quickly.
"It appeared in front of me," Emilia replied, swallowing hard.
She focused on the invisible panel, reading carefully.
A few seconds passed, and her expression shifted from confusion to disbelief.
"How did you even find something like this?" she whispered. "This is insane."
"Second assessment," Leon replied with a grin. "And as expected, do not talk about it. I will only show it this once."
"Alright," Emilia nodded seriously. "But the [Hatching Time]... it is absurd. Even elves do not live that long."
"Lifespan in [Eternal Ascension] works differently," Leon explained. "If the circumstances are right, we can live for hundreds of thousands of years."
Leon had only lived fifteen years in this world so far, but he knew the truth.
There were players who had existed for centuries. The gods themselves were effectively immortal, untouched by time.
His goal was not just power for the sake of power.
He wanted to grow strong so that he and his companions could live freely in this world. No fear. No chains.
No matter how dangerous [Eternal Ascension] was, it also held wonders beyond imagination.
"We can rest for now," Leon said. "After that, if you want, we can visit the [Myriad Arena] before heading out."
"The [Myriad Arena]?" Emilia’s eyes sparkled instantly. "Now you have my attention.
Leon’s ID was already known throughout the [Lower Domain].
Hiding forever was impossible. Sooner or later, players would seek him out.
The [Myriad Arena] was the perfect place for that. Players could fight freely to test their abilities, and more importantly, he could hide his ID inside.
Meanwhile, outside the inn, chaos erupted.
Guards rushed through the streets, weapons drawn.
Players stopped what they were doing, looking around warily. Some activated defensive spells, while others prepared to flee.
The aura explosion had been felt across large portions of the city.
No one could have guessed that the source was a single unhatched egg.
Leon frowned slightly as he thought about it. The egg still had over 4,000 years left before hatching.
If it could cause such a disturbance now, what kind of monster would emerge when it finally hatched?
After around an hour of resting, talking, and eating a simple meal, Leon and Emilia left the inn.
Instead of heading out of the city, Leon led Emilia deeper inside.
"Our goal is simple," Leon explained as they walked. "Win ten matches in a row. It might get harder, but we will get a very good reward. After that, we can leave."
"Alright," Emilia nodded confidently.
The deeper they went, the more crowded the streets became.
Eventually, they reached a massive gate standing in the middle of the city.
The structure was enormous, carved with ancient symbols and glowing faintly with divine energy.
Tens of thousands of players gathered around it.
"Is that..." Emilia began.
"The [Myriad Arena]," Leon said with a grin. "One of the most popular places in this city."
Players entered and exited constantly, excitement written on their faces.
Some looked confident. Others looked defeated.
Leon and Emilia approached the gate, blending into the crowd.
No one paid them any attention. There were simply too many people.
"Once we enter, we will be separated," Leon said. "Just focus on winning ten matches in a row. That is all. I believe in you."
"I got this," Emilia said proudly. "No mercy."
Leon smiled slightly.
Truthfully, he had nothing to worry about. Emilia was absurdly strong.
Her spells alone could annihilate most opponents before they even had a chance to react, and even if they dodged, how could they even hope to harm her?
And so, without hesitation, the two stepped through the gate.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Myriad Arena", a space created by the "Heavenly One" to allow players to fight each other.]
[Win your matches, and you shall be blessed with rewards!]

Leon and Emilia approached the gate, blending into the crowd.
No one paid them any attention.
There were simply too many people.
"Once we enter, we will be separated," Leon said.
"Just focus on winning ten matches in a row.
That is all.
I believe in you."
"I got this," Emilia said proudly.
"No mercy."
Leon smiled slightly.
Truthfully, he had nothing to worry about.
Emilia was absurdly strong.
Her spells alone could annihilate most opponents before they even had a chance to react, and even if they dodged, how could they even hope to harm her?
And so, without hesitation, the two stepped through the gate.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Myriad Arena", a space created by the "Heavenly One" to allow players to fight each other.]
[Win your matches, and you shall be blessed with rewards!]

chapters.title: Chapter 97: Entering the Myriad Arena, Beating Opponents
paragraphs: Ding!
[Do you wish to show your ID in the "Myriad Arena"?]
[Do note that selecting "no" will result in your name being used.]
Leon barely needed a second to think. The only thing that mattered here was making sure his ID would not be displayed.
The name "Celestial" carried far more weight than "Leon Rykard."
If that ID appeared in the arena, it would spread instantly. Players would recognize it, whisper about it, and soon enough, chaos would follow.
Some would challenge him, hoping to make a name for themselves. Others would try to recruit him at any cost.
There would also be those far more dangerous, players who believed that killing him might grant them whatever rewards he had obtained to trigger such a massive global announcement.
They did not know what he had gained, but most assumed it had to be something extraordinary.
And they were not wrong. Still, there were limits.
No one could take the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos] egg from him, nor could anyone steal the SS-Level sub-talent [Master of Elements]. Those were bound to him in a way no player could interfere with.
The only thing that could potentially be taken, if someone got extremely lucky, was the [Enhancement Frenzy Liquid].
Leon frowned slightly as another thought crossed his mind.
’Players with a very high [Slaughter Meter] could be troublesome.’

The [Slaughter Meter] was dangerous in its own way. The higher it became, the more powerful the [Slayer] titles a player could obtain. Those bonuses could turn already strong players into terrifying opponents.
Even so, Leon did not hesitate.
"No."
Ding!
[The name "Leon Rykard" will be shown to the others. Do note that you may allow players to check your ID at any time.]
[The "Heavenly One" reserves a special reward for players who win 10 matches in a row.]
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly at the final line. Almost no one ever reached that reward.
The rules were cruel by design. Each victory made the next fight harder. Losing even once reset the entire streak. All progress vanished in an instant.
Leon also knew something most players did not. The tenth match was completely unfair.
It was designed that way on purpose, and it was the reason nearly everyone failed.
The opponent, the conditions, and the pressure all stacked against the challenger.
And yet, Leon needed that reward. No matter how difficult it was, he could not afford to ignore it.
At least the arena was not lethal in the usual sense.
Dying inside the [Myriad Arena] did not mean true death. Players who lost would respawn outside the arena gates.
The price, however, was heavy. Anyone who died was barred from entering again for an entire week.
Leon had no intention of waiting that long.
He planned to crush his opponents quickly, cleanly, and without hesitation.
He believed Emilia would do the same. And so, without further delay, the system moved him forward.
Fwoosh! Ding!
[You will be teleported to the "Myriad Arena" for your first match.]
[May the will of the "Heavenly One" be with you.]
Leon felt his vision blur for a brief moment.
There was no pain, no discomfort, just a smooth sensation of being pulled away.
When his sight returned, he found himself standing in the arena.
He opened his eyes fully and took in his surroundings.
The battlefield resembled a refined version of a Roman gladiator arena.
Massive stone walls surrounded the circular field, carved with ancient symbols that radiated faint divine power.
Above, instead of an open sky, a vast holographic projection shimmered, shifting slowly like living clouds.
Leon glanced toward the stands. There were only a handful of spectators.
Around five people sat scattered across the seats, their attention focused entirely on the center of the arena.
"Come on, deal with it!"
"First match. You can do this!"
Their voices echoed faintly, filled with excitement.
It was obvious who they were cheering for. They were not here for Leon.
The reason was simple. Neither Leon nor his opponent had any fame. Early matches rarely drew crowds, especially when no known names were involved.
Leon knew that would change quickly if he kept winning. The closer someone got to the tenth match, the more spectators gathered. By then, the arena would be packed.
After all, few things entertained players more than watching others fight.
Leon turned his gaze forward. His opponent stood across from him.
Appraisal!
[ID: MomoTheApe]
[Level: 27]
[Talent: ???]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
As expected, the arena restrictions were in place. Leon could only see the opponent’s name and level. Everything else was hidden.
Still, he did not need more. Voices rose again from the stands.
"There is no way that guy can beat you. He is two levels lower and from a low-level world."
"Unlucky kid. He ran into a tank as his first opponent."
MomoTheApe stood tall, clearly enjoying the encouragement.
He wore thick, heavy armor that covered his body completely. His head resembled that of a monkey, marking him as a member of the ape race.
He rolled his shoulders slightly, confidence radiating from him.
"Sorry, human," Momo said calmly. "But you are going to be an insignificant stepping stone in my—"
Powerful Fireball!
A massive sphere of fire began forming at the tip of the staff.
The temperature in the arena rose instantly. The air itself trembled as overwhelming mana surged outward.
The spectators fell silent. Momo’s confident expression froze.
He could only stare as the fireball continued to grow, its size and density far beyond what he expected.
The pressure pressing down on him felt suffocating, as if his lungs were being crushed.
This was the result of Leon’s spell being enhanced by the SS-Level sub-talent [Master of Elements].
The fire element responded perfectly, its rank pushed to an absurd level. The result was raw, terrifying destructive power.
Leon gently swung his staff.
Fwoosh!
The fireball shot forward like a meteor.
"Damn it!" Momo roared.
The explosion engulfed him completely. Flames swallowed his armored body in an instant, melting metal and flesh together. There was no scream, no struggle.
The battle ended immediately.
Ding! Fwoosh!
[You have won your first match.]
Leon felt the familiar pull once more as the arena vanished around him. Darkness surrounded him briefly as he waited for the next match to be prepared.
It did not take long. Moments later, he was sent back into the arena.
This time, more people were watching. Around ten spectators sat in the stands, their curiosity clearly piqued.
"Die!"
The shout came the instant Leon appeared.
His opponent was a girl from the wolf race. Her sharp ears twitched as she exploded into motion the moment the match started.
Power surged through her legs as she closed the distance in an instant.
SLASH!
Her daggers flashed, aimed straight for Leon’s vital points. She intended to end the fight before he could even react.
But Leon had already seen it coming.
Shadow Slash!
His body melted into darkness as the skill activated. The attack passed harmlessly through empty space.
"Huh?"
The wolf girl barely had time to react.
Leon emerged behind her, sword already in motion. The blade cut cleanly through her body, overwhelming power slicing through her defenses without resistance.
Her form split apart before she could even scream.
Ding!
[You have won your second match.]
Leon stood calmly as the arena began to fade again.
"Well," he muttered with a faint grin, "this should not be too difficult."
After all, he had already killed a dragon. Compared to that, this was nothing.
